1	Source: Hacker News
2	Title: Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed
3	URL: https://www.kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro
4	Published: 2026-10-23T16:59:08Z
5	Content: full article text
6	
7	Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
8	We're introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in our new K3.1 series and our most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window. It delivers substantial improvements across coding, 3D creation, financial research, and other agentic capabilities.
9	We are also releasing Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which delivers 2-3× the speed of K3.1 Pro for more responsive interactions.
10	Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed are available today on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API. The full model weights will be released by Nov 4.
11	Advancing the Frontier of Open Intelligence
12	Kimi K3.1 Pro is a post-trained version of Kimi K3, with substantially larger post-training compute. To enable large-scale joint RL across hundreds of downstream domains, we optimized every layer of the stack — the RL framework, long-context inference, training efficiency, sandbox infrastructure, rollout scheduling, and a shared platform for environment quality checks — so that each increment of RL compute delivers stable, predictable returns. As a result, K3.1 Pro achieves consistent gains in every domain.
13	Across coding, agentic, and knowledge benchmarks, K3.1 Pro matches or approaches the strongest proprietary models. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which evaluates coding agents on realistic, resource-constrained terminal tasks using strict task-specific tests, K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and narrowly behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%). And on Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon, our internal benchmark that tests coding agents' multi-step execution, tool use, and end-to-end problem solving across diverse engineering domains, K3.1 Pro scores 61.2%, above K3's 55.95%.
14	Coding
15	K3.1 Pro covers the full range of coding work, from quick fixes in real codebases to full-project builds. It also brings a more considered visual style to games and web experiences, and knows how to build them with the right tools.
16	K3.1 Pro works effectively across game engines such as Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot, combining them with web search and 3D generation to create complete experiences. Its front-end pages, interactive Three.js scenes, and 3D assets show stronger composition, typography, animation, and polish. The examples below were created end to end by K3.1 Pro:
17	K3.1 Pro's long-horizon coding capabilities are also strengthened through large-scale reinforcement learning. In one internal test, it built a human walking dynamics simulator with integrated training and evaluation pipelines on top of human-atlas, an open-source anatomical model of the human body comprising 296 skeletal components, including cartilage, and 402 muscle components. Across 167 missions and 420 independent reviews, it analyzed experimental results, diagnosed problems, and iteratively refined the walking controller, enabling the simulated human to go from collapsing within seconds to walking continuously with alternating strides for 11.2 seconds. When reward shaping failed to improve arm motion, K3.1 Pro did not simply keep adjusting the reward: it ran open-loop probes of the simulator's dynamics, identified and corrected 36 errors in shoulder-muscle moment-arm calculations, and then retrained the controller.
18	3D Modeling and Design
19	K3.1 Pro is strong at 3D creation and spatial reasoning. On BenchCAD, which tests 3D reconstruction from multi-view renderings through CAD code generation, K3.1 Pro scores 92.7% with tools, approaching the performance of Claude Opus 5.5 (96.2%) and GPT-6 Astra (95.9%). From a text brief, sketch, or reference image, it can infer shape, proportions, and spatial relationships to create usable 3D models. It also has a stronger grasp of existing asset libraries and model collections.
20	K3.1 Pro particularly excels at parametric modeling, from mechanical parts and architectural models to configurable products and custom furniture. Without MCP connectors, it can write and run scripts for tools like Blender and CAD software to build and refine assets, edit components, and adjust geometry, materials, and scene layout.
21	Below are examples of 3D assets K3.1 Pro created for brand films, games, and interactive web experiences:
22	3D Make is now live on kimi.ai and the Kimi app — preview and edit your 3D models online, download them ready for 3D printing, or export them as videos or Live Photos to share anywhere.
23	Finance
24	With stronger reasoning and agentic capability, K3.1 Pro is capable of end-to-end delivery of complete financial workflows. K3.1 Pro achieves state-of-the-art results on OfficeQA Pro v2 (64.4), which tests complex fiscal data analysis over real financial documents through retrieval, cross-document verification, and multi-step numerical reasoning. K3.1 Pro also improves over K3 on Frontier Finance, which measures support for complete investment workflows from screening to profitability analysis.
25	K3.1 Pro also improves significantly across all our internal finance benchmarks:
26	- Financial Modeling evaluates formula linkage, financial logic, and final workbook quality in real-world modeling tasks. K3.1 Pro improves on K3 by 7.2 points.
27	- Financial Research evaluates whether models can produce auditable research under evidence and cutoff constraints. K3.1 Pro improves on K3 by 11.6 points.
28	- Business Operation evaluates long-horizon management and decision-making in a simulated business environment. K3.1 Pro achieves about 4.2× K3's performance.
29	Financial analysis and investment research demand a high degree of factual accuracy. To address this, we made targeted improvements to K3.1 Pro's factual accuracy on real-world tasks and challenging prompts. On Kimi Hallu Bench Hard bench, an internal benchmark designed to stress-test factual accuracy, its claim-level hallucination rate fell from 23.4% for K3 to 8.3%, while the share of responses containing at least one factual error was just 42.4% of its predecessor's rate. (The evaluation is a stress test for factual accuracy, with examples deliberately crafted to probe situations where models are prone to errors. The reported rates do not represent overall error rates in daily use.)
30	The cases below show how K3.1 Pro handles financial modeling, investment analysis, and source-grounded research in practice:
31	Cybersecurity
32	As K3.1 Pro became more capable, we spent a correspondingly larger share of our effort understanding where cyber capability comes from, and how much of it we can control. We therefore analyzed and evaluated K3.1 Pro's vulnerability research capabilities, and applied targeted controls during training to reduce potential misuse risk while preserving general usefulness.
33	Identifying and removing cyber-related data. During development, we observed vulnerability research performance improving steadily as post-training scaled. Tracing the source of this trend, we found that cyber-related content was embedded within the general mid-training corpus, and cyber-related tasks were present in the RL environment mix — a natural byproduct of training on broad data. In preliminary experiments on internal models, we found that without data removal at either the mid-training or the RL stage, downstream cyber capability would increase substantially. These findings gave us a concrete lever for control. For the open-weight release of K3.1 Pro, we identified and removed cyber-related data from both training stages, while retaining the general-purpose coding tasks needed for model usefulness. We will continue to apply appropriate controls at every training stage, of which cyber-related data identification and restriction is one example.
34	Evaluation and results. After data cleaning, we evaluated K3.1 Pro on xdev-bench-hard, our in-house benchmark of expert-curated, source-code-based vulnerability discovery and exploitation tasks, calibrated to provide meaningful differentiation at our current capability level. Most tasks faithfully reproduce recently disclosed vulnerabilities in software such as the Linux kernel, Node.js, JavaScriptCore, Exim, and VirGL, with mitigations enabled. Each task provides the vulnerable source code, a short bug hint, and the corresponding binary; the agent must develop an exploit, achieve arbitrary code execution in a separate sandbox, and retrieve a secret string for automated verification. We report pass@3 over a random subset of runs, with no hard timeouts or output token limits.
35	On xdev-bench-hard, the checkpoint without these risk-reduction measures — no cyber-related data removal at mid-training and no cyber-related RL environment filtering — solves 90.5% of problems at pass@3; the final K3.1 Pro reaches 81.0%. The comparison shows that data removal meaningfully reduces cyber capability relative to what the same training pipeline would otherwise produce. At the same time, K3.1 Pro improves substantially over its predecessor, indicating that stronger general coding and long-horizon debugging capabilities generalize to cyber tasks even after targeted data removal. K3.1 Pro's cyber capability remains behind that of frontier proprietary models that have been publicly available for at least three months. We will keep evolving our internal benchmarks so that evaluation stays informative as model capabilities continue to advance.
36	Open-weight principles. These evaluations frame our open-weight release decision. First, we aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability. K3.1 Pro's offensive cyber capability is, by design, below what our pipeline can produce, and remains behind that of frontier proprietary models. Second, we intend to progressively raise the cyber capability available in open weights. We believe making K3.1 Pro available in a non-discriminatory way benefits people who need dual-use capabilities for defensive purposes. When a capable model is open and runs on infrastructure its users control, many more teams gain the means to audit the code they maintain — including legacy systems that rarely receive dedicated security reviews. We believe that letting this capability diffuse gradually — rather than concentrating it in a few proprietary systems — ultimately makes all software more secure.
37	Availability
38	Kimi K3.1 Pro rolls out today across the Kimi product family: on Kimi.ai and the Kimi mobile apps, Kimi Work and Kimi Code, and through the Kimi API.
39	Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026.
40	Kimi Enterprise administrators can enable K3.1 Pro for their organization; access is off by default at launch.
41	Details for each channel:
42	- Kimi Agents: Download or update to the latest Kimi app from your mobile app store, available on iOS, Android, and HarmonyOS, or visit kimi.ai.
43	- Work with Kimi K3.1 Pro: Download the latest Kimi Work desktop app, version 3.1.0 or later, available for Windows and Apple silicon Macs.
44	- Code with Kimi K3.1 Pro: Run Kimi Code and select Kimi K3.1 Pro using the /model command.
45	- Build with the Kimi API: Visit the Kimi API Platform and select kimi-k3.1-pro / kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed. Zero Data Retention is available for API customers.
46	- Bring Kimi to your organization: Kimi Business provides enterprise-grade data privacy and member management, with complete separation between personal and organization accounts. Visit the pricing page and select “Get Kimi Business” to subscribe for your team.
47	Benchmarks
48	Footnotes
49	Unless otherwise specified, all Kimi K3.1 Pro results reported below are obtained with the reasoning effort set to 'max', temperature = 1.0, and top-p = 0.95.
50	Coding benchmarks
51	- Terminal-Bench 4.0. Kimi K3.1 Pro is evaluated with the Claude-Code harness. The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is taken from the release blog (https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017). All remaining scores are taken as the maximum value reported in either their blog posts or the official Terminal-Bench 4.0 leaderboard (https://www.tbench.ai/).
52	- Terminal-Bench Science 0.1. Kimi K3.1 Pro is evaluated with the Claude-Code harness. Our internal evaluation of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 yields a score of 9.3; However, an older version, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, scores 15.7 on the official Terminal-Bench Science, so we report 15.7 here; all remaining scores are from the official Terminal-Bench Science leaderboard (https://www.terminal-bench-science.ai/).
53	- DeepSWE v1.1. Kimi K3.1 Pro is evaluated with the Claude-Code harness. All scores are taken from each model's respective technical report. GPT-6 Astra(https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra/). Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1(https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5-system-card and https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-5-1-mythos-5-1-system-card); DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news261017/); GLM-5.3 (https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.3).
54	- SWE-Marathon v1.1. Kimi K3.1 Pro is evaluated with the Claude-Code harness. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is evaluated with the ClaudeCode harness. All other scores are taken from the official SWE-Marathon leaderboard (https://www.swe-marathon.org/).
55	- PostTrainBench. Kimi K3.1 Pro and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 were evaluated internally on v1.2 using the Claude-Code harness and H20 GPUs instead of H100 GPUs. For stable evaluation, all judge models used DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at maximum effort, which best matched the official GPT-5.6-Terra (xhigh) judge in testing. Other scores are from the official leaderboard (https://posttrainbench.com/).
56	- ProgramBench (binary score). We report binary scores rather than raw ProgramBench scores: a task receives a score of 1 if its ProgramBench score is ≥95%, and 0 otherwise. Kimi K3.1 Pro is evaluated with the Claude-Code harness. The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and GLM-5.3 scores are taken from the release blog (https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017); all remaining scores are from the Vals ProgramBench leaderboard (https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/programbench).
57	- Internal Coding Bench: Kimi Code Bench 2.0 and Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon. Kimi K3.1 Pro is evaluated with Claude-Code harnesses; All other models are evaluated at their max-effort setting. Note that proprietary model testing may involve some fallback behavior.
58	- BenchCAD. Open models are evaluated by us on 1,000-case subsets randomly sampled from the full 17,900-case Vision2Code dataset, at maximum reasoning effort. With-tools results use the Claude Code harness; without-tools results use single-shot generation with the official BenchCAD prompts and scoring pipeline. Scores for Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 are taken from the Claude Opus 5.5 System Card; GPT‑6 Astra’s with-tools score is taken from its official report. GPT‑6 Astra has not reported a without-tools score and is marked “—”.
59	Agentic benchmarks
60	- BioMysteryBench dataset is drawn from the official v11 release, with Kimi K3 as the judge model. We evaluate Kimi K3.1 Pro with Kimi Code, GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 with Claude Code, and GPT-6 Astra with Codex. Scores for the C

1	Source: Hacker News
2	Title: OBS Studio 33
3	URL: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/releases/tag/33.0.0
4	Published: 2026-10-24T04:49:58Z
5	Content: full article text
6	
7	33.0 New Features
8	- Updated CEF from 127/6533 to 150/7871 [WizardCM] (#13900)
9	  - This is a massive update to the underlying framework used for browser sources and docks from the July 2024 release to September 2026
10	  - All of this work is on the backend and should be invisible to users. Please be sure to report any new weirdness or problems you run into with browser sources!
11	- Complete overhaul to plugin loading [FiniteSingularity/PatTheMav] (#13594)
12	  - First-party plugins are now in a new folder named core
13	  - Third-party plugins have an updated installation location and folder structure
14	  - Existing third-party plugins will continue to load from the legacy locations until OBS Studio 34.0
15	  - More information is available in our knowledge base article
16	- Improved how source snapping works in the preview [Warchamp7] (#12298)
17	  - New visual indicator added
18	  - Sources now snap along the entire axis instead of only when directly touching
19	  - Sources no longer snap to hidden sources
20	- Improved behavior of spinboxes for number values [Warchamp7] (#12337)
21	  - Typing is no longer mysteriously blocked in some situations
22	  - Numbers are no longer cut off in some situations
23	  - Values now update only after pressing Enter and Enter does not close the window
24	  - Holding Shift + Up/Down now advances multiple steps at a time
25	  - Dragging the cursor inside the input but outside the text itself now works properly
26	- Enabled NVENC on Arm64 [RytoEX] (#13827)
27	33.0 Changes
28	- Added a check for encoders being missing when loading a profile [derrod] (#11340)
29	- Added support for newest NVIDIA Broadcast SDKs for NVIDIA Audio Effects and Video Effects [pkviet] (#13838)
30	- Added hotkeys for controlling audio monitoring of a source [Warchamp7] (#13599)
31	- Changed Safe Mode to not start WebSocket Server [FiniteSingularity/RytoEX] (#13984)
32	- Fixed issues with groups in Studio Mode [Warchamp7] (#11092)
33	  - Fixed moving sources inside a group causing them to glitch out in Program
34	  - Fixed moving sources inside a group showing up live in Program
35	- Adjusted naming of Window Capture methods on Windows [Penwy] (#12047)
36	- Improved detection of fullscreen games for Game Capture [Kira-NT] (#10880)
37	- Improved transparency handling for macOS Screen Capture [jcm93] (#13030)
38	- Scaled simple output recording audio bitrate by channel count [nickvonkaenel] (#13311)
39	- Removed support for Ubuntu 24.04
40	33.0 Bug Fixes
41	- Added a startup error if obs-transitions failed to load [notr1ch] (#13321)
42	- Improved file splitting for Hybrid MP4/MOV [derrod] (#13386)
43	- Fixed outputs getting stuck running when a bad rescale output resolution is set [suogesi] (#13375)
44	- Fixed monitoring icon state getting desynced when using third-party tools or websockets [prgmitchell] (#13822)
45	- Fixed a crash on macOS 27.2 when starting OBS Studio [RytoEX] (#14070)
46	- Fixed potential crash when shader cache file is invalid [notr1ch] (#13538)
47	- Fixed a potential crash on Linux when USB mic is removed [R0te/RytoEX] (#13922)
48	- Fixed a potential crash when renaming a source with the Add Source window open [Warchamp7] (#13800)
49	- Fixed a potential deadlock during video/audio tasks [exeldro] (#13579)
50	- Fixed an issue with B-frame offset calculation in AMF that could cause streams to disconnect [lexano-ivs] (#13762)
51	- Fixed PipeWire screencast sources being duplicated in studio mode [tytan652] (#13673)
52	- Fixed a potential crash when switching off a newly created profile [Warchamp7] (#13182)
53	- Fixed a source toolbar crash when source type is missing [Penwy] (#13539)
54	- Fixed profile import failing on paths with a trailing slash [Ushkalovk] (#13863)
55	33.0 Developer Information
56	- Added frontend event and output signal for replay buffer saving [Penwy] (#8955)
57	- Added guidance regarding the theme system to the top of all theme files [Warchamp7] (#13733)
58	- Added ability to set a file extension filter for OBS_PATH_FILE_SAVE path types [FiniteSingularity] (#10190)
59	- Added obs_frontend_is_safe_mode for first-party plugins
60	  - Third-party plugins are not loaded at all in Safe Mode
61	- Added versions to Flatpak plugin extension point [tytan652] (#13735)
62	- Added obs_canvas_video_active() to check if the video of a canvas is active [exeldro] (#13110)
63	- The minimum supported versions of Visual Studio, Windows SDK, and clang-format have been increased. Previous versions may continue to work, but will no longer be tested/supported. It is recommended that build environments are kept up-to-date with the project's toolchain.
64	- Changed obs_canvas_reset_video() to allow resetting a canvas's video when any other canvas's video is active, but not its own video [exeldro] (#13110)
65	- Updated libnsgif to 1.0.0 [RytoEX] (#11178)
66	  - This is a breaking change for any plugins using libobs/graphics gs_image_file
67	- Clarified documentation for obs_module_unload [notr1ch] (#13327)
68	- Required MbedTLS 3 and exclude 4 or later [tytan652] (#13799)
69	- Removed support for FFmpeg 6.x and 7.x [RytoEX] (#13964)
70	- Removed support for Qt 6.4-6.9 [RytoEX] (#13969)
71	- Fixed repeated preview enable/disables not working [WarmUpTill] (#12580)
72	- Only emit core signal handlers for public canvases [tt2468] (#13574)
73	- Deprecated unused hidden API for sources [derrod] (#13122)
74	- Deprecated APIs for audio source monitoring_type [Warchamp7] (#13599)
75	  - This is replaced by a new monitoring_enabled boolean

2	Title: Physicists trap a single antimatter particle for a month
3	URL: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/physicists-trap-a-single-antimatter-particle-for-a-month/
4	Published: 2026-10-21T19:40:01Z
5	Content: full article text
6	
7	You can’t hold antimatter in your hand or even in a regular laboratory apparatus. As soon as antimatter meets matter, the two tend to annihilate each other. This makes studying antimatter tricky. But now physicists have managed to trap a single subatomic particle of the stuff for months at a time in a way that allows them to study its quantum states.
8	Further investigations using the trap might reveal the secret of why the world around us is made of matter and not antimatter, when things could have presumably gone either way.
9	Every normal particle of matter has an antimatter counterpart with equal mass but opposite charge. To build their trap, physicists started with atoms of sodium 22, a radioactive isotope with a half-life of about two and a half years. When one of these atoms decays, it emits a positron—the antimatter counterpart of the electron.
10	On supporting science journalism
11	If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
12	“The big challenge is to persuade these positrons to slow down and then capture them,” says Gerald Gabrielse, a physicist at Northwestern University, who oversaw the project. The team reported its achievement on Wednesday in Physical Review Letters.
13	The first step is to send the positrons through the crystal lattice of a sliver of cold tungsten. As the particles go pinballing through the material, they slow down and lose energy. “Every time they bang into something, there’s a chance of annihilation, but it doesn’t always happen,” Gabrielse says. “If they make it to the end, they get popped out.”
14	Next, the physicists steer the positrons along a channel using electromagnetic fields. Eventually the particles end up in a vacuum, just three tenths of a degree Celsius above absolute zero, trapped by an electric field on top and bottom and a magnetic field on the sides. “If you want to hold on to antimatter, you have to hold it in a container without walls,” Gabrielse says.
15	This method allowed the researchers to isolate and study a solitary, lone positron for a month—and could let them do so indefinitely.
16	The researchers intend to use their trap to make precise measurements of the positron’s magnetic moment—basically the strength and orientation of its magnetic field. To do this, they must determine two things: the energy needed to flip the direction of the positron’s spin and the energy needed to make it jump from its ground state to its first excited state.
17	Using a similar trap setup, Gabrielse and his team have already measured the magnetic moment of an electron to a precision of one part in 10 trillion. Taking the equivalent measurement for a positron will allow them to make a crucial comparison. “We’re looking to see if they have an exactly opposite magnetic moment,” Gabrielse says. That’s the prediction of the Standard Model of particle physics. If the two have different values, however, this could help explain why our universe is made of matter instead of antimatter.
18	Just after the Big Bang, scientists think there were roughly equal amounts of the two. Most of the matter and antimatter must have annihilated, but a small excess of matter was somehow left over to seed the stars and planets we see. The magnetic moment measurement is just one of many realms where physicists are seeking differences between matter and antimatter to account for this profound discrepancy.
19	“Turn every particle to its antiparticle, look at physics through a mirror (flipping left and right) and press the ‘rewind button’ to reverse the flow of time,” says Roni Harnik, a theoretical physicist at the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory in Batavia, Ill., who was not involved in the project. “Our most basic theories say that physics stays the same.”
20	If it turns out things are different—that the positron, for instance, has a different magnetic moment than the electron—then we’d have a hint about how matter won out.
21	“This is an exciting development,” Harnik says, “that will enable us to test a basic symmetry.”

2	Title: Canadians are running out of time to oppose Bill C-22
3	URL: https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2026/10/canadians-are-running-out-time-oppose-dangerous-c-22-surveillance-bill
4	Published: 2026-10-22T22:43:19Z
5	Content: full article text
6	
7	Canada’s Parliament is debating a massive expansion of surveillance powers that will threaten the privacy and security of millions of people. Bill C-22, also called the Lawful Access Act, has already passed the House of Commons, and is now before the Canadian Senate.
8	Canadians still have an opportunity to speak out and stop this dangerous legislation. The Canadian Civil Liberties Association (CCLA) is urging all Canadians to sign its petition opposing the bill. (The petition on CCLA’s website is governed by CCLA’s privacy policy.)
9	As we wrote earlier this year, Bill C-22 gives the government new powers to force digital services—including telecom companies, messaging apps, and more—to help with government surveillance. Worse, it allows Canada’s Minister of Public Safety to order companies to create a backdoor to their services for law enforcement, as long as it doesn’t lead to a “systemic insecurity.” That’s a clear recipe for weakening the encryption we all rely on.
10	It also requires services to retain metadata for up to a year, which reveals who people communicate with, where they go, and what services they use, even when they are not suspected of any crime.
11	Researchers at CCLA and Citizen Lab published a detailed analysis of C-22 and its serious constitutional and cybersecurity problems. The analysis points out that the bill needs more than cosmetic changes—it calls for entirely withdrawing Part 2 of Bill C-22, the section that establishes the surveillance and data retention regime.
12	Bill C-22 could also expand the sharing of Canadians’ personal data with foreign law enforcement, including the United States. Canada has been negotiating a cross-border data-sharing agreement with the U.S. that would allow American police to get information about Canadian internet users without any Canadian court oversight.
13	Some Canadian senators have already expressed concerns about the bill, and rightly suggested, as CCLA and Citizen Lab have, that it may not be compatible with privacy protections in the Canadian constitution.
14	If you’re in Canada, read and sign CCLA’s petition opposing Bill C-22 today. Don’t let the Senate allow this dangerous expansion of government surveillance to become Canada’s new reality.
15	Canadians: defend your privacy and security

2	name: gather
3	description: Collect candidate items for ONE section of today's issue from the day's news bundle and write them to a candidates file. Use as a gatherer subagent launched by publish-issue; it does not select, draft or publish.
4	allowed-tools: Read, Write, Glob, Grep
5	---
6	
7	# The gatherer
8	
9	You collect raw material for one section of today's issue. You do not decide what gets published
10	and you do not write for readers. The editor selects and writes; a verifier checks. Your job is to
11	hand them accurate facts, each tied to the exact text it came from.
12	
13	Your task gives you the section, today's date, the bundle folder and the output path. Read
14	`newspaper.toml` (audience, `editorial.exclude_topics`) and the "What goes in" and "What stays out"
15	parts of `.claude/skills/editor/SKILL.md` first.
16	
17	## The bundle is your only source
18	
19	`<bundle>/index.md` lists every item collected today, one line each: `[id] time · title — summary`.
20	`<bundle>/text/<id>.txt` holds each item's full article (or only its feed summary, marked so in its
21	header). You have no web access. Never state a fact that is not in a text file.
22	
23	## How to work
24	
25	1. Scan `index.md` for items that belong to your section. Headlines from Israeli outlets, world
26	   outlets and specialist feeds all count; the section is about the subject, not the outlet.
27	2. Group items that report the same event: that is one candidate with several sources.
28	3. Open the text files of each candidate's items. Take the facts from the text: who decided or did
29	   what, numbers with their context, dates, what happens next.
30	4. For each fact, copy a short supporting quote exactly as it appears in the file (up to about 25
31	   words), with its id. The verifier and a script check that the quote is really there.
32	5. Skip what the editor rules exclude (rhetoric, leaks, unconfirmed claims, polls, excluded topics)
33	   into `dropped`. When unsure, keep it and say why in `notes`.
34	6. Skip stories already published in the previous issue (listed in your task) unless something new
35	   was decided or measured since; then the candidate is the new development.

But Collins' announcement, which The Wall Street Journal first reported, did not mention that while tariffs would be removed for some Canadian products, new ones would be added to the list of goods subject to steep U.S. duties. The White House announced the new tariffs less than an hour after Collins touted the new exemptions to the tariffs, which are unpopular in the state where she's fighting for reelection.
President Donald Trump earlier Friday signed a proclamation "removing certain products" from the list of items that he slapped 50% tariffs on over the summer using a 96-year-old trade law.
But he is "replacing those products with certain valves, carpets, waste products, and others," according to a White House fact sheet detailing the proclamation.
The changes are being made to "further refine the scope of the tariffs on certain Canadian products," according to the fact sheet, which does not mention Maine.
The new additions and removals from the list of goods covered by the "Section 338" tariffs will take effect Oct. 30, four days before the Nov. 3 U.S. election, the fact sheet said.
Asked what Collins had agreed to in her conversations pushing Trump administration officials for lower tariffs on products affecting her state, her spokeswoman Phoebe Keller told CNBC that the senator "requested exemptions for products that are important to Maine and will continue to do so."
Before the fact sheet was made public, Collins' office sent a press release crediting the senator with securing the new tariff exemptions on "nine categories of products crucial for Maine's agricultural industries."

Title: Oil price rises above $117 a barrel amid fears US will renew strikes on Iran
URL: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/23/oil-five-month-high-fears-us-renews-strikes-iran
Published: 2026-10-23T16:48:28+00:00
Content: full article text

Oil has hit its highest level in more than six months as fears of fresh escalation in the Middle East conflict grip the energy markets.
Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, rose by about 3.5% on Friday to pass $117 a barrel at one point – its highest level since April.
The jump came after Tehran said it would attack oil facilities, undersea cables, datacentres and AI facilities in the Gulf region if a new US-Israeli offensive was launched against Iran.
Richard Hunter, of the broker Interactive Investor, said: “Widespread reports that the US is considering renewed military strikes on Iran after the midterm elections rather than pursuing a diplomatic route was enough for the price to pop, after what many had considered would be a brief conflict is now in its eighth month.”
The oil price later eased back slight to sit about 2.7% up at just over $116 a barrel. Brent crude had traded at about $72 a barrel back in February, before the Iran war began, but soared to touch $126 a barrel by the end of April.
Tensions in the region have been rising this week and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed to have struck four commercial ships in the strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. The US state department ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia, which has faced continued attacks from Houthi rebels in Yemen.
Susannah Streeter, the chief investment strategist at the broker Wealth Club, said fears were rising that American and Israeli forces would be ordered to launch strikes on Iran’s energy infrastructure after the US elections on 3 November.
She added: “At the same time, the attacks on Saudi Arabia’s facilities by Houthi rebels have intensified this week, and for ships attempting to cross the strait of Hormuz, it’s still a dangerous journey, with projectiles still being fired.”
Streeter said Ukraine’s bombardment of Russian diesel refineries was also adding to supply concerns.

Households will need to earn less than £110,000 to qualify for the government's new loan scheme for first-time buyers, or £140,000 for homes bought in London.
As first reported by The Times, external, the earnings limits are expected to be confirmed at the Budget next week.
The Your First Home scheme will offer government-backed equity loans worth 20% of new-build properties in England bought from participating developers.
The loans, which will also be subject to an initial interest-free period, are designed to help people buy a home with deposits as low as 2.5%.
Previous schemes to help first-time buyers did not restrict eligibility by income but faced criticism for stoking house prices by allowing relatively wealthy households to borrow more.
Unveiling the Your First Home Scheme at last month's Labour conference, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it would focus on those who "really need support".
The Times reported that ministers had initially decided to set the earnings limits at £90,000 for homes outside outside London and £110,000 in the capital, before concluding this would deny access to too many middle-earning couples, such as teachers and nurses.
The government has also argued that the scheme will help to boost housebuilding, after ministers conceded they are set to miss a target to build 1.5 million homes in England by the next election.
Help to Buy

Developers taking part in the scheme will also be asked to contribute towards running costs.
The Home Builders Federation, which represents developers, has welcomed the plans and urged the government to move quickly to set up the scheme.
The Conservatives have however branded the proposals a "colossal admission of failure" of Labour's housebuilding record, and expressed concerns that the new developer levy could push up the price of new homes.
Like the Help to Buy scheme launched under the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government, the scheme will use equity loans, which are linked to changes in the value of properties they are used to purchase.
That scheme, which initially ran between 2013 and 2021, enabled all home purchasers to put down a 5% deposit on a newly built home worth up to £600,000.

1	Source: Hacker News
2	Title: Bringing uv and ty together
3	URL: https://astral.sh/blog/uv-ty-integration
4	Published: 2026-10-20T21:30:56Z
5	Content: full article text
6	
7	TL;DR: Experimental uv-ty integration is now available, enabling first-class support for Python
8	scripts (on the CLI and in the editor) and a unified uv check command.
9	This is a step towards an integrated Astral toolchain, one that uses a shared understanding of your project to enable entirely new capabilities.
10	At Astral, we build high-performance tools for the Python ecosystem: uv, our package manager; Ruff, our linter and formatter; and ty, our type checker and language server.
11	Historically, each Astral tool has focused on making a different component of Python development more productive. But we see an opportunity to further Python by unifying traditionally separate capabilities into an integrated toolchain.
12	Our vision for the Astral toolchain is simple: while each tool should be individually usable, useful, and interoperable with the rest of the ecosystem, they should be even more capable when used together.
13	Today, we’re announcing an experimental integration between uv and ty, available in preview. uv understands your Python project’s environment and dependencies, while ty understands your code. By combining the two, we can unlock new functionality beyond what either tool can provide individually.
14	PEP 723 enables Python scripts to declare their dependencies and Python version requirements through inline metadata. uv already uses this metadata to prepare an environment when running a script. Now, ty can use this metadata to understand your scripts.
15	On both the command line and in the editor, ty now uses inline metadata to discover scripts throughout your project and leverages uv to prepare an environment for each script. These environments allow ty to check your scripts against their declared requirements.
16	Scripts can have different requirements within the same repository. Each script is checked against its own dependency declarations, even if those dependencies or Python requirements differ from the surrounding project.
17	Declare dependencies inline with PEP 723, save to sync with uv, and use ty’s completions, hover information, and Go to Definition capabilities in your editor.
18	When the integration is enabled in your editor, ty automatically invokes uv to prepare the script’s environment in the background, which it uses to provide type checking, code navigation, and completions based on the script’s declared requirements.
19	Over time, we plan to enable script support by default, and enable automatic environment setup for standard Python projects.
20	uv check introduces a unified diagnostic interface to uv, starting with support for ty. Over time,
21	we plan to support Ruff in uv check to unify linting and type checking into a single command.
22	Running uv check will automatically prepare your project’s environment, install the required
23	dependencies, and check your project with ty. It “just works.” (If you never run uv check, nothing
24	changes for your uv experience; the ty binary is installed separately on first invocation.)
25	With uv check, you can check individual packages, or an entire workspace. In a workspace, use
26	uv check --package <name> to select an individual package, or uv check --all-packages to check
27	every package. uv uses your workspace configuration to determine what to check, so the command stays
28	the same as your workspace grows.
29	Sync your project’s dependencies and type-check your code with a single command.
30	Standalone PEP 723 scripts have independent environments and are checked separately. Use
31	uv check --script example.py to check a script using its declared requirements.
32	uv check automatically uses the ty version recorded in your project’s lockfile. Commit your
33	project configuration and lockfile, and developers and CI running uv check will share the same ty
34	version without separately maintained pins.
35	The ty pre-commit hook also uses uv check under the
36	hood to run ty before each commit over your Python project. By using uv check, the hook
37	automatically sets up the environment for ty from your project’s dependency declarations.
38	The uv-ty integration is powered by
39	uv workspace metadata, which gives ty a
40	structured view of your project or script’s packages, dependencies, and Python environment. ty then
41	uses this information to provide type checking and editor features that reflect the configured
42	environment.
43	For PEP 723 scripts, ty invokes uv to prepare the script’s environment, which includes installing declared dependencies. As dependency installation can require execution of third-party Python code, automatic environment setup is currently opt-in.
44	To try the integration for
45	PEP 723 scripts in VS Code, install uv
46	and the ty VS Code extension,
47	then enable the uv integration in your VS Code settings.json.
48	{
49	  "ty.experimental.useUv": "on"
50	}
51	You can also check your project and its PEP 723 scripts from the command line with:
52	TY_UV=scripts ty check
53	Running uv check enables the integration
54	automatically and requires no additional configuration.
55	Support for PEP 723 scripts and the uv check command requires uv 0.12.3 or later, and ty 0.0.76 or
56	later.
57	This integration is experimental, and we’d love your feedback as we refine the experience.
58	While this initial support largely leverages uv’s environment capabilities to power ty execution, we’re also working on a new category of checks that combine uv’s knowledge of your project’s dependencies with ty’s understanding of your code (e.g., to detect unused dependencies), which we’ll cover in a future post.
59	And, in parallel, we’re continuing toward ty’s stable release.
60	Thank you for building with us!
61	Thanks to Aria Desires, Micha Reiser, and Zsolt Dollenstein from the Astral team for implementing the features behind this integration.
62

3:description: Core editorial rules for this newspaper — what goes in, what stays out, how items are written, and the exact issue file format. Read before selecting, drafting, verifying or correcting any issue.
4----
5-
6-# The editor
7-
8-You are the editor of a one-page daily newspaper. There is no human editor; you are it, and a
9-separate verifier (the `fact-check` skill) checks your work before anything is published.
10-Preferences for this particular paper (name, language, sections, length, sources, audience,
11-excluded topics) live in `newspaper.toml`. Read it first. Where it and this file disagree on a
12-preference, `newspaper.toml` wins. The rules below are the paper's character; they are not
13-preferences.
14-
15-The paper exists to tell readers what happened and what changed, in as few words as that takes,
16-without manipulation. A reader should finish the page calmer and better informed, not more
17-anxious or more angry.
18-
19-## What goes in
20-
21-Every candidate item must pass all three tests:
22-
23-1. **Impact** — it changes something for many people, or for a few people a great deal.
24-2. **Durability** — it will still matter in a month. Things that will be forgotten by tomorrow stay out.
25-3. **Verifiability** — the core facts are in the day's bundle (`work/<date>/`), and either come
26-   from an official primary source (a government decision, a central bank statement, a statistics
27-   bureau release, a court ruling, a published paper, release notes, a security advisory) as reported
28-   in the bundle, or are reported by at least two independent outlets in the bundle. Facts that are
29-   undisputed matters of record (a vote's result, a published figure, a launch that happened) need
30-   one reputable outlet.
31-
32-Then rank by impact and keep between `issue.min_items` and `issue.max_items`. Never pad with items
33-that fail the tests; with dozens of outlets in the bundle, a normal day has enough that pass. Below
--
43:## What stays out
44-
45-- **Rhetoric.** Statements, threats, endorsements, accusations, "X slammed Y", reactions to reactions.
46-  A statement goes in only when the statement itself is the official act (a formal announcement of a decision).
47-- **Leaks and anonymous sourcing.** "Sources say", "officials familiar with", interrogation transcripts,
48-  reports of what someone allegedly said. Wait for the official record.
49-- **Allegations against individuals** outside a formal legal proceeding. Arrests, indictments, court
50-  rulings and their official statements are in scope; describe them in the neutral terms the court or
51-  police use, never more.
52-- **Unverified claims of attacks or casualties**, including claims by a party to a conflict that the
53-  other side or independent sources have not confirmed.
54-- **Polls and horse-race coverage**, predictions, speculation, "what this could mean".
55-- **Sponsored or promotional content** of any kind, including press releases presented as news
56-  without independent substance.
57-- **Anything in `editorial.exclude_topics`.**
58-
59-## How an item is written
60-
61-- **Headline**: one declarative sentence stating the fact. No questions, no adjectives of intensity
62-  ("dramatic", "shocking", "historic"), no puns, no quotes as headlines.
63-- **Body**: two to four sentences. What happened, who it affects and how much, what happens next
64-  officially (a date, a vote, a deadline) if known.
65-- **Numbers always carry context**: a denominator, a comparison period, a target range, or a base
66-  rate. "1.6% annual inflation, inside the 1%–3% target" — never a number alone.
67-- **Conflicting figures**: give both, each attributed to its source ("local authorities: 53; earlier
68-  reports: at least 18"). If figures conflict too widely to report without choosing a side, drop the item.
69-- **Casualties and harm**: official figures, attributed. No graphic detail. No victim imagery in words.
70-- **Attribution in text**: name who decided, measured or reported. No links in the issue body.

המסחר בבורסת תל אביב ננעל במגמה שלילית, המושפעת מהירידות החדות שנרשמו בסוף השבוע בוול סטריט (בעיקר במניות הטכנולוגיה) וממתיחות גיאופוליטית. מדד ת"א 35 איבד כ-1% מערכו, ומדד ת"א 125 נחלש בכ-0.8%. לעומתם, מדד ת"א 90, שמוקדם יותר שהה סביב רמות הבסיס, הצליח להפגין יציבות יחסית ורשם ירידה מזערית של 0.1% בלבד.
בחלוקה סקטוריאלית, את המגמה השלילית הוביל סקטור הטכנולוגיה שצולל ב-1.9%. אחריו בלטו לשלילה מדד תשתיות אנרגיה וסקטור הקלינטק שירדו בכ-1.7%, ומדד הביומד שנחלש ב-1.3%. גם מדד המניות הדואליות הכביד על השוק עם ירידה של 1.2%.

בסיכום שבועי, המסחר בבורסת תל אביב ננעל במגמה מעורבת, תוך פער בולט בביצועים בין המדדים המרכזיים. בעוד שמדד ת"א 35 חתם את השבוע בירידה של 1.4% ומדד ת"א 125 הרחב איבד 0.6%, מדד ת"א 90 בלט לחיוב עם זינוק שבועי של 2.2%.

Title: דליה גוררת את ניו מד ורציו לבוררות בינלאומית בלונדון על עסקת הגז מלוויתן
URL: https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001560603#utm_source=RSS

המאבק על עסקת הגז הגדולה ביותר שנחתמה בין מאגר לוויתן ליצרן חשמל פרטי עובר לזירה המשפטית. משק אנרגיה המחזיקה בתחנת הכח דליה, מדווחת הבוקר כי דליה הגישה אתמול בקשה לפתיחת הליך בוררות בבית הדין הבינלאומי לבוררות בלונדון (LCIA) נגד ניו מד אנרג'י, שבשליטת קבוצת דלק של יצחק תשובה, ונגד רציו אנרגיות משק אנרגיה
● יו"ר רשות ני"ע מזהיר: "החלפת ריכוזיות בנקאית בריכוזיות מוסדית אינה תחרות" 
● הכנסות של כ-840 מיליון דולר: מאגר הגז לוויתן צפוי לשבור שיא הרבעון 
במסגרת הבוררות מבקשת דליה שלושה סעדים הצהרתיים: כי ביטול העסקה מצד המוכרות של הגז ב-24 בספטמבר ניתנה שלא בהתאם להסכם ובניגוד להוראות הדין, ולכן חסרת תוקף, וכי גם אם ההודעה תקפה, ההסכם לא בוטל, שכן אישור רשות התחרות ניתן בתוך מסגרת הזמנים שנקבעה בו. דליה מבקשת שההסכם למעשה ייכנס לתוקף.
פרטי עסקת הענק: גז ל-20 שנה
ההסכם נחתם במאי ונועד לספק גז לשתי תחנות כוח חדשות שדליה מקימה - "דליה 2" במתחם צפית ו"אבשל" במתחם אשכול, תחנת הכוח הגדולה ביותר שהופרטה מחברת החשמל. מדובר בהתקשרות ל-20 שנה, מ-2030 ועד 2050, במחיר של 4.7 דולר ליחידת חום, שייפתח למשא ומתן ב-2041 בטווח של 10% לכל כיוון. ניו מד, המחזיקה בכ-45% ממאגר לוויתן, אחראית לכשלושה רבעים מהיקף העסקה, ורציו ליתרה.

Title: What next for France as riots rattle markets? Three questions facing investors ahead of more protests
URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/24/france-riots-paris-unrest-debt-budget.html
Published: 2026-10-24T06:23:02+00:00
Content: full article text

France's unrest is fueling investor concerns over the country's fiscal outlook, after borrowing costs hit their highest level since 2002 earlier this week.
With further demonstrations planned, fund managers are assessing whether prolonged disruption could weaken growth, undermine confidence and make it harder for the government to deliver planned budget savings.
Rating agency Moody's on Friday kept its Aa3 credit rating on France, a level it still deems "high grade," but maintained its negative outlook on the nation.
"The negative outlook reflects the increased risk that the fragmentation of France's political landscape will continue to impair the functioning of the country's legislative institutions," Moody's said in its report.
Moody's noted that it could return France's outlook to stable if its institutions can narrow its budget deficit.
France's government aims to reduce the budget deficit to 5% of GDP in 2027, from a projected 5.4% in 2026. The National Assembly is due to resume debating on the budget's tax measures, which are intended to generate savings, on Oct. 27 but opposition lawmakers are resisting the plans.
Alain Durré, head of EMEA economic research at Natixis CIB, said the government was determined to prevent a sharp rise in borrowing costs.
Durré said the government could try to stick to its fiscal targets by invoking Article 49.3 — which allows it to push a bill through the assembly without a final vote unless lawmakers can pass a no-confidence motion — or by using executive ordinances.
That could help settle nerves and restore investor confidence, Durré added, noting that recent pressure on French sovereign debt has been driven primarily by tactical portfolio reallocations, with traditional buy-and-hold investors "still sitting on the sidelines."

Title: Volvo Cars plunges 24% as CEO says China sales slump came 'faster than we thought'
URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/volvo-cars-q3-earnings-job-cuts.html
Published: 2026-10-23T15:40:54+00:00
Content: full article text

Volvo Cars said Friday it plans to cut 2,500 jobs after a sharp decline in its Chinese market weighed on third-quarter earnings.
The Swedish automaker reported an operating loss of 5.6 billion Swedish kronor ($563.7 million) in the third quarter, down from an operating profit of 6.4 billion Swedish kronor in the previous period.
The company, which is owned by China's Geely Holding, cited a deteriorating environment led by "tougher" market conditions in China and the U.S., which "negatively affected free cash flow."
Volvo Cars shares were 24.2% lower at the end of the trading session.
"It's really a lot about the Chinese market, of course, where the change has come faster than we thought, and really now we can see that selling global cars developed in Europe and China will not work, and then this is affecting all the Western players in China," Volvo Cars CEO Håkan Samuelsson told CNBC on "Squawk Box Europe," on Friday.
Chinese consumers are now looking for "domestic alternatives," which have become stronger and more competitive, the CEO said. "We need a new strategy in China... it has to be a more regional structure, a more empowered region, and we need regionally adapted cars."
He added that costs must be competitive and that Volvo Cars needs to share some platforms with its Chinese parent company Geely, and develop key software in China that includes infotainment and driver-assistance systems. "If you don't have that, I think you cannot sell cars in China."
Volvo Cars' revenues in China fell almost 50% year-on-year as premium brands faced "hypercompetition" from new Chinese rivals, which also put severe pressure on pricing, the company said.

Title: American Express is cutting 5% of its workforce to 'prepare for AI'
URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/american-express-job-cuts.html
Published: 2026-10-23T18:57:48+00:00
Content: full article text

American Express is cutting thousands of employees as the leading credit card company prepares for artificial intelligence to take over more of its internal processes.
Amex is eliminating 5% of its global workforce and taking a $336 million restructuring charge, CEO Stephen Squeri told analysts Friday on the company's third-quarter earnings call. The firm had almost 77,000 employees at the end of 2025.
Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec told CNBC in an interview that the restructuring was to make American Express "leaner, more agile, and also to prepare for AI."
"You don't want to automate processes that are not optimally structured," Le Caillec said. "So what we're doing here is to reduce layers and increase spans of controls, so that we can automate and take advantage of AI in the coming quarters and the coming years."
The Amex announcement reflects a broader trend across financial services, where banks are working to replace repetitive roles with AI automation. On Thursday, Barclays confirmed plans to trim 5,000 jobs — also roughly 5% of its staff — in another tech-driven cost initiative. The moves come even as the sector is enjoying robust profits from growing consumer spending and resilient credit.
During the analyst call, Squeri said the charge was to improve the company's efficiency.
"We've got good momentum, but to accelerate innovation and win over the next few years, we needed to become [a] more agile and efficient organization," Squeri said.

Title: Defense giant Saab sees orders triple after Gripen fighter jet deal with Ukraine

Published: 2026-10-23T16:26:17+00:00
Content: full article text

Swedish defense giant Saab reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and revenue on Friday, as new orders more than tripled from a year earlier, boosted by a deal to supply Gripen fighter jets to Ukraine.
New orders came in at 65.8 billion Swedish kronor ($6.6 billion), up from 20.9 billion kronor a year earlier, beating FactSet expectations of 56.4 billion kronor.
Third-quarter sales reached 20.6 billion kronor, ahead of FactSet expectations of 20 billion kronor. Earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) came in at 1.95 billion kronor, also beating forecasts of 1.9 billion kronor.
Stockholm-listed shares closed 1.8% higher Friday, amid a mixed defense sector. The Stoxx 600 index ended the session down 0.3%.
The results come as European governments race to turn defense spending pledges into military capability.
Saab's order intake included a 24.6 billion kronor contract for 16 Gripen E fighter jets with the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration for Ukraine, signed in June and booked in the third quarter. Deliveries are scheduled for 2029-2030.
"The growing customer demand is reflected in major contract awards, including Gripen for Ukraine, GlobalEye and an order related to Germany's new frigates," CEO Micael Johansson said in a statement.
Orders booked in the quarter also include a 10.1 billion kronor order for its military surveillance aircraft GlobalEye to an undisclosed customer in the Middle East, and an 8.7 billion kronor order to equip warships for the German Navy.

8	US First Lady Melania Trump has secured an agreement between Russia and Ukraine to temporarily halt military operations in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, the White House announced on Friday. The intent is to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and evacuate civilians trapped near the front line.
9	The localised ceasefire is scheduled to begin on 29 October, with both sides agreeing to suspend military action in the southern Ukrainian city and establish a designated safe passage for residents wishing to leave, according to the White House.
10	Oleshky lies on the Russian-occupied eastern bank of the Dnipro River, opposite the Ukrainian-controlled city of Kherson. Before Russia's full-scale invasion, it had approximately 24,000 residents. According to White House estimates, only 1,700 to 2,000 remain, including around 50 children.
11	The announcement comes amid a deepening humanitarian crisis in Oleshky, where residents face severe shortages of food, clean water and medicine, while attempts to escape have exposed civilians to mines and drone attacks.
12	Speaking exclusively to Euronews on 13 October, Tetiana Hasanenko, head of the Oleshky city military administration, described a city devastated by more than four years of Russian occupation.
13	"The city is practically destroyed," she said. "There is almost no building that has not been damaged."
14	Hasanenko estimated that around 2,000 people remained in Oleshky, including 35 children who, she said, were unable to leave.
15	She described residents surviving on a single meal a day, sometimes consisting of only a few spoonfuls of grain, while others had resorted to eating weeds.
16	Melania Trump's role in the agreement
17	According to the White House, the First Lady and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leaders to negotiate the terms of the humanitarian pause, including its timing, technical procedures and implementation.
18	Melania Trump initiated discussions with both sides, acting in what the White House described as the formal role of "Exclusive Intermediary".
19	"The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster," she said.
20	The First Lady described the remaining population as predominantly elderly residents in urgent need of medical attention and basic supplies, with limited electricity, mined roads and continuing military attacks complicating humanitarian access.
21	She argued that her intervention had been essential to securing the agreement and making aid deliveries and evacuations possible.
22	Under the proposed arrangements, civilian representatives from Ukraine and Russia will visit residents in their homes to assess their needs and coordinate assistance.
23	Those wishing to leave will be offered transportation to their preferred destination, with Melania Trump saying she expected some to choose Ukraine and others Russia.
24	The First Lady also said she had secured the participation of an impartial American media organisation to accompany and document the operation, although the White House did not identify the organisation.
25	The statement did not specify how long the ceasefire would last or provide detailed security guarantees for those involved in the humanitarian operation.
26	A 25-kilometre 'road of death'
27	Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since the first days of Moscow's full-scale invasion in February 2022. The city was further devastated by flooding following the destruction of the Kakhovka dam in June 2023, which submerged large parts of the area and damaged already fragile infrastructure.
28	In her exclusive interview with Euronews, Hasanenko described how residents attempting to flee had been forced to walk approximately 25 kilometres towards the village of Radianske, crossing heavily mined territory exposed to drone attacks.
29	Many were already physically weakened by hunger, she said, while some who managed to escape subsequently returned with food for children and elderly relatives unable to make the journey themselves.
30	Hasanenko said people had been killed by mines along the route, with some bodies left unrecovered.
31	"This road really is a road of death," she said.
32	She also accused Russian forces of targeting food deliveries and punishing residents suspected of receiving assistance from Ukrainian troops.
33	Euronews has been unable to independently verify conditions inside Oleshky, which remains under Russian occupation and inaccessible to independent journalists.
34	A humanitarian operation in occupied territory
35	The White House said the initiative originated during a private discussion at Melania Trump's Fostering the Future Together event in New York, held during the 81st United Nations General Assembly.
36	Both countries then assigned teams to coordinate the arrangements, including demining, according to the White House.
37	The agreement, if implemented, could provide a rare opportunity to reach civilians who have spent years largely cut off from regular humanitarian assistance.
38	But with Oleshky remaining under Russian military control, questions remain over how safe access will be guaranteed, how the suspension of hostilities will be monitored and whether residents will be able to leave freely for their chosen destinations.

7	דובר צה"ל ודוברות שב"כ עדכנו הלילה (בין שישי לשבת), מעט לפני חצות, על פתיחה במבצע בחברון שעתיד להימשך כמה ימים - בעקבות הפיגוע בצומת יהודה שבו נפלו סמ"ר רון יונתן רויטמן וסמל יובל שי סוילם. מדובר במבצע רחב שבו יסרקו הכוחות עשרות יעדים, ובהם כאלה מהחמולה שממנה יצאו המחבלים. "כוחות צה"ל, שב"כ, מג"ב איו"ש ומת"ק יהודה בפיקוד חטיבת יהודה פתחו במבצע לסיכול טרור במרחב העיר חברון, ממנו יצאו שני המחבלים שחוסלו במסגרת ההיתקלות בה נפלו שני לוחמי צה"ל ונפצעו נוספים", נמסר.
8	לפי הודעת צה"ל ושב"כ, "הכוחות החלו לסרוק כעת באופן ממוקד ויסודי את כלל התשתיות במרחב לאיתור ונטרול תשתיות טרור ואמצעי לחימה, ולתחקר עשרות רבות של חשודים. המבצע ממוקד ומתוחם לאזור ממנו פעלו המחבלים ועתיד להימשך מספר ימים. החל מתחילת המבצע, התושבים שגרים במרחב פעילות הכוחות יוכלו לצאת מהמרחב דרך שלוש נקודות ייעודיות לאחר תחקור ובידוק. כל אדם שלגביו יעלה חשד במהלך הבידוק יועבר לתחקור כוחות הביטחון".
9	עוד נמסר: "המבצע הינו המשך ישיר של שורת פעולות התקפיות לסיכול טרור שננקטו מהבוקר, ביניהן: מיפוי בתי המחבלים, כתר במרחב חברון וחלחול, חסימות ופעילויות סיכול בכפרים בגזרה. בנוסף למאמץ עיצוב המרחב, במסגרתו מסירים תשתיות לא חוקיות שיכולות להוות סיכון ביטחוני במרחב ההיתקלות. כוחות הביטחון פועלים בשעות אלו בעשרות יעדים לסיכול טרור לאורך כל גזרת יהודה ושומרון, וימשיכו לפעול בהתקפיות ויוזמה לצורך הגנה, סיכול טרור והסרת איומים על אזרחי מדינת ישראל".
10	הפיגוע התרחש הבוקר בצומת יהודה, בכביש 35 סמוך לחברון. שני מחבלים פלסטינים הגיעו למקום ברכב, ירדו ממנו ופתחו באש לעבר כוח צה"ל. בחילופי האש, שנמשכו יותר מ-20 דקות, נהרגו סמ"ר רון יונתן רויטמן (23) מאשקלון וסמל יובל שי סוילם (20) מהוד השרון, ושלושה לוחמים נוספים נפצעו באורח קל. במהלך ההיתקלות הגיעו לזירה כוחות נוספים, ובהם סגן מפקד גדוד ארי ומפקד פלוגה, שאיגפו את המחבלים וחיסלו אותם.
11	במערכת הביטחון מעריכים כי שני המחבלים התכוונו לבצע פיגוע משמעותי נגד אזרחים, וכי ההיתקלות עם הלוחמים מנעה מהם להמשיך בדרכם לעבר הצירים הראשיים. ברכבם נמצאה כמות גדולה של תחמושת, ולפי התחקיר הראשוני הם היו חמושים בין היתר ברובה M16 ובאקדח. בשלב זה עדיין לא ברור אם המחבלים פעלו ביוזמתם או הופעלו בידי גורם חיצוני, והחקירה נמשכת בניסיון לברר מה היה היעד שאליו התכוונו להגיע.
12	שני המחבלים שחוסלו הם חמודה אל-ג'עבה ופיראס אל-ג'עבה, בני 27 מחברון, שהשתייכו לאותה חמולה והתגוררו בסמיכות זה לזה. כבר בשעות שלאחר הפיגוע פעלו כוחות הביטחון למיפוי בתיהם, ובמקביל הוטל כתר על חברון וחלחול. בצה"ל הפעילו גם את נוהל "בריח אפור", שבמסגרתו נבדקים כלי רכב פלסטיניים המגיעים לצירים הראשיים. ההיערכות הורחבה גם לגזרות ג'נין, שכם ויריחו, מחשש לפיגועים נוספים.
13	ראש הממשלה בנימין נתניהו, שהגיע לזירת הפיגוע עם שר הביטחון ישראל כ"ץ, הודיע כי ישראל מתכוונת להרחיב את פעילותה בשכונות שמהן יצאו המחבלים. נתניהו אמר כי בכוונתו ליישם באזור את מודל הפעילות הצבאית במחנות הפליטים ביהודה ושומרון, הכולל כניסה נרחבת של כוחות, פינוי תושבים ואיתור תשתיות טרור. "אנחנו נפנה את התושבים, אנחנו נעבור בית בית, נוציא שם גם את כלי הנשק, וכל תשתיות הטרור יטופלו וייהרסו", אמר.
14	שני הלוחמים שנפלו שירתו בגדוד ארי (775) של חטיבת החילוץ בפיקוד העורף, שהוקם בשנה האחרונה על רקע הצורך בהגדלת סדר הכוחות הלוחם. הגדוד, החמישי בחטיבה, החל רק במהלך השבוע האחרון את התעסוקה המבצעית הראשונה שלו, לאחר כמה חודשים של הכשרה. רויטמן וסוילם הם שני הנופלים הראשונים של הגדוד מאז הקמתו. בעקבות הפיגוע אמר הרמטכ"ל אייל זמיר כי צה"ל נערך מבעוד מועד לאפשרות של הסלמה ביהודה ושומרון, תגבר את כוחותיו והפעיל באזור גם את מפקדת אוגדה 98.

7	US first lady Melania Trump helped broker a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia in the city of Oleshky, the White House announced Friday. The localized truce, according to the White House, is slated to begin on October 29.
8	What do we know so far about the ceasefire deal in Oleshky?
9	The Ukrainian city occupied by Russia on the frontline of the war faces a humanitarian crisis and only around 2,000 people still live there. Prior to the war, the city had a population of around 24,000.
10	Oleshky has been under blockade since 2025 and was first occupied when Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
11	The city is located in southern Ukraine, just 9 kilometers (around 5.6 miles) from the major city of Kherson.
12	"Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food and clean water," Melania Trump said in a statement. "The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks."
13	Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, thanked the first lady for securing the deal.
14	"Under our agreement: first a ceasefire will be put in place; second, humanitarian aid will be delivered to Oleshky; and third, civilians will be allowed to move freely out of Oleshky," Lubinets said in a video message posted on Telegram. "The operation will be carried out gradually and is extremely challenging to implement."
15	Russia also confirmed the agreement and said it will halt fire earlier than what the White House announced at 0400 local time (0100 GMT) on October 27.
16	According to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights, residents in Oleshky say Russian occupying forces prevented them from leaving the city. Oleshky residents also say Russia has used civilians to shield military positions in the city — a war crime under international humanitarian law.
17	Fresh Ukraine talks expected in Abu Dhabi next month
18	The ceasefire deal in Oleshky comes as US, Ukrainian and Russian negotiators are expected to meet in Abu Dhabi next month to discuss ending the war.
19	"The plan is to meet in the first half of November, and as early as possible, of course," Zelenskyy told the US conservative Hudson Institute think tank.
20	In comments to Russian state news outlet TASS, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov also said preparations are underway for a three-way meeting in mid-November. Russian President Vladimir Putin said security would be a main topic for the Abu Dhabi talks.
21	"That is the security of both countries, Russia and Ukraine, after there has been a transition to a peace settlement," Peskov said.
22	The Kremlin spokesperson said Russia only sees the Europeans at the table during a later stage in the talks. European leaders such as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz have said Europe must be involved in future Ukraine peace talks.
23	"It is clear that the architecture of European security cannot be discussed without other participants," Peskov added.
24	US President Donald Trump has grown increasingly frustrated at Zelenskyy, and is pressuring him to "make a deal."
25	Trump has blamed Ukraine for rising diesel prices in the US, as the US-Israeli war against Iran has caused the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and drove up the cost of gas at the pump for American consumers.
26	Trump has backed a deal to buy diesel from Russia to lower prices at fuel pumps, drawing criticism from Ukraine. The Kremlin said Friday that the first tanker of Russian diesel has set sail for the US despite the backlash from Ukraine.
27	Ukraine still dealing with Starshield issues as Trump defends Musk
28	Most recently, there has been controversy that tech billionaire Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of the Starshield military communications system that Ukraine relies on, possibly with the backing of Trump.
29	Trump has denied that he ordered restrictions on Starlink. He also defended Musk in comments to reporters on Friday and said, "Elon will never do anything wrong."
30	"You know, whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn't make any difference," Trump said. "I guess the bottom line, he put it back."
31	Meanwhile, Zelenskyy and Ukraine said Friday that the system was still being throttled in Ukraine.
32	"It works, but it's still limited," Zelenskyy told US broadcaster ABC News.
33	A source in Ukraine's Defense Ministry told AFP news agency and other news outlets that Ukrainians were witnessing "instances of signal loss" when using Starshield.
34	"There is currently no confirmation that the restrictions have been lifted," the source added.

8	The Trump administration is lifting some of its 50% tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterm elections, after a Republican candidate in a key US Senate race said she had lobbied for the change.
9	From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on products including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment", the White House said on Friday.
10	Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race to keep her seat in Maine, first announced the exemptions, saying they would help her state's agriculture industry.
11	The US imposed a 50% levy on $20bn (£15bn) worth of Canadian goods after trade talks between the two countries collapsed in August.
12	Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures in response to the US tariffs, which Prime Minister Mark Carney said were "necessary to protect our workers".
13	Last month, Carney matched the US tariffs "dollar for dollar" after the breakdown in talks. Trump had imposed them for what he called "unequal treatment" of US car, dairy and alcohol exports.
14	The White House said that, while tariffs would be lifted from some items, including some packing crates and boxes, they would be introduced on other items such as carpets and "waste products".
15	It said the action reflected US President Donald Trump's "continued efforts to defend American workers and ensure fair trade".
16	Trump "continues to address Canada's discriminatory treatment of US commerce", White House spokesman Matthew Middleton said.
17	Canada's internal trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said: "While we assess these latest steps, Canada stands ready to work constructively and in good faith towards a more mutually beneficial trading relationship that respects Canada's interests."
18	The White House's announcement comes less than a fortnight before the US midterm elections, which will determine whether Trump's Republican Party or Democrats will control Congress, impacting the remaining two years of his term.
19	Collins said she had repeatedly asked senior Trump officials for tariff relief and that she would "continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbour, ally and largest trading partner".
20	She wrote on X that the tariff exemptions were on products that were "crucial to Maine's agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers".

11	But he is "replacing those products with certain valves, carpets, waste products, and others," according to a White House fact sheet detailing the proclamation.
12	The changes are being made to "further refine the scope of the tariffs on certain Canadian products," according to the fact sheet, which does not mention Maine.

14	Asked what Collins had agreed to in her conversations pushing Trump administration officials for lower tariffs on products affecting her state, her spokeswoman Phoebe Keller told CNBC that the senator "requested exemptions for products that are important to Maine and will continue to do so."

20	White House spokesman Matthew Middleton told CNBC in a statement Friday afternoon that Trump's latest tariff proclamation is part of his efforts to "address Canada's discriminatory treatment of U.S. commerce."

8	The Trump administration wants to block the certification of the Senate election in Alaska if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses, arguing that another candidate with the same name may confuse voters.

3	URL: https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/24/debt-moodys-spares-france-a-brief-respite-not-a-vote-of-confidence
