Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
- Date:
- October 22, 2026
- Source:
- The University of Queensland
- Summary:
- A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.
- Share:
The largest collection of exploding white dwarf stars ever compiled is providing fresh evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force responsible for the Universe’s accelerating expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a central assumption of modern cosmology and could help scientists better understand how the Universe evolves.
An international research team led by scientists at the University of Queensland’s School of Mathematics and Physics brought together observations of 2,884 Type Ia supernovae. These powerful stellar explosions serve as important tools for measuring distances across the Universe, allowing astronomers to trace its expansion history.
PhD candidate Ryan Camilleri said the project establishes a new international standard for supernova cosmology. By bringing decades of measurements into a unified dataset, researchers have created their most detailed picture yet of how cosmic expansion has changed over time.
“We’ve rebuilt 3 decades of astronomical observations into a single, consistent framework,” Mr. Camilleri said.
“We combined our data with other cosmic measurements including relic light from the Big Bang and maps of how galaxies are distributed through space.
“Instead of confirming the standard model of cosmology which assumes dark energy is fixed and unchanging, we have more evidence that dark energy may change over time.”

Plaid Cymru ministers favour burying cables underground instead.
Plans for a network of pylons in the Towy Valley have faced a fierce local backlash with local Plaid politicians speaking out against the proposals.
The company behind the plans, Green Gen Cymru, said it welcomed the consultation and that it supported using "the right infrastructure in the right place".
Prohibiting the use of large steel lattice pylons for new lines up to 132 kilovolts was a Plaid Cymru manifesto pledge before May's Senedd election.
Launching a consultation on its policy on Friday, the Welsh government said undergrounding electricity circuits could "reduce the visual impact of electricity infrastructure, helping to protect landscapes and local amenity".
It also said that burying cables could make them less vulnerable to severe weather and could reduce the potential impact on birds and other wildlife.
However, the consultation document also acknowledges that undergrounding was "generally considered more expensive to install and maintain and could create construction impacts during installation".
The government's policy would allow for wooden poles or "equivalent, less intrusive infrastructure" to be used to support overhead cables where undergrounding isn't feasible.

7	מתי המעבר לשעון חורף 2026?
8	שעון החורף ייכנס לתוקפו בלילה שבין 24 ל-25 באוקטובר 2026 (בין שבת לראשון) בשעה 02:00 יחזרו מחוגי השעון שעה אחת אחורה, כך שנוכל לישון שעה נוספת. שעון החורף יימשך עד המעבר לשעון קיץ ב-26 במרץ 2027.
9	איך אדע שהשעון המעורר שלי יעבוד בזמן הנכון?
10	ברוב המוחלט של הסמארטפונים השעה מתעדכנת באופן אוטומטי, כך שאין צורך לבצע שום שינוי. אם אתם לא בטוחים שהטלפון שלכם מעדכן אוטומטית את השעה, יש להיכנס להגדרות הטלפון ולשנות בהגדרות את הגדרת תאריך ושעה מ"כיוון אוטומטי" לידני ותחת "שעון מקומי" לבחור ב"ירושלים". 
11	בלילה של החלפת השעון נישן שעה יותר או פחות?
12	השעון זז שעה אחורה, לכן למעשה נרוויח שעת שינה נוספת.
13	למה עוברים לשעון חורף?
14	העברת הזמן לשעון חורף ולשעון קיץ מתבצעת בישראל לפי הגרסה האחרונה של חוק קביעת הזמן משנת 2013. לפי חוק קביעת הזמן, כמדי שנה, ביום ראשון האחרון של חודש אוקטובר מזיזים את השעון בישראל שעה אחת אחורה. הזזת השעון מסמנת גם את חילופי העונות ומזג האוויר שמתקרר, ומשמעותה המיידית היא זריחה של השמש מוקדם יותר - ושקיעתה מוקדם יותר בהתאם.
15	איך שעון החורף משפיע עלינו? 
16	בחורף, כשאור השמש מוגבל ויש יותר שעות חושך ביממה, רמות הורמון המלטונין בגוף עולות ואנו עשויים להיות מנומנמים ועייפים יותר. תפקיד המלטונין (מכונה גם "הורמון חושך") הוא לווסת את מחזוריות השינה, מתוך מטרה להתאים את השינה לשעון הביולוגי. גם הסרוטונין, הורמון נוסף האחראי בין היתר על מצב הרוח והרגשות, קשור על-פי מחקרים באופן ישיר למידת החשיפה שלנו לאור. הירידה בכמות הסרוטונין בגוף בחורף עלולה לגרום למצב רוח ירוד ומדוכדך.
17	מה הקשר בין שעון החורף לפעילות היומיומית שלנו?
18	שינוי השעות בין הקיץ לחורף מאפשר להתאים את פעילות בני האדם לשעות האור והחושך. בקיץ למשל אנו מרוויחים שעת אור מאוחרת, ובחורף אנו מתעוררים בדרך כלל בשעות שבהן השמש מתחילה לזרוח, וכך לא מתפספסות שעות חיוניות לניצול על-ידי האדם או המשק.
19	מדוע לא להשאיר את שעון הקיץ כל השנה?
20	בשל היתרונות הגלומים בשעון קיץ, רבים תומכים בהנהגתו למשך כל השנה. המתנגדים לשעון החורף טוענים כי הוא מקצר את זמן האיכות של הורים עם ילדיהם, מגביר את הסיכון לתאונות דרכים עקב נהיגה ממושכת יותר בשעות החשיכה, מעוות את השעון המקומי לעומת השעונים באירופה וביתר העולם ומייקר את הוצאות המשק במאות מיליוני שקלים.
21	מה קורה במדינות אחרות בעולם? 
22	כמה מדינות הפסיקו להזיז את השעון בקיץ ובחורף, בהן רוב מדינות אסיה, אפריקה ודרום אמריקה. גם בארה"ב יש גורמים הלוחצים להפסיק את שינוי השעון בחורף. בנוסף, הפרלמנט האירופי הצביע ב-2019 בעד ביטול המעבר העונתי לשעון קיץ – כך שכל מדינה יכולה להחליט אם להישאר כל השנה באזור הזמן הרגיל שלה או לעבור באופן קבוע לשעון קיץ. הסוגיה עלתה גם בישראל פעמים רבות, אך לבסוף החליטה הכנסת להשאיר את המצב כפי שהוא כיום.
23	מתי יסתיים שעון החורף?

7	חודש וחצי אחרי שילדה את בתה הבכורה, נועה (31), תושבת שכונת מונטיפיורי בתל אביב, כבר חוששת לצאת איתה לטיול בשעות הערב. היא מתגוררת בבניין יוקרה עם שומרים, משלמת דמי ניהול גבוהים, אבל לדבריה, גם האבטחה אינה מצליחה להעניק לה תחושת ביטחון. בבקרים היא נתקלת במזרקים בגינה שמתחת לביתה, ובשעות הערב, היא מספרת, דרי רחוב רבים מסתובבים באזור. 
8	כך למשל, לפני כחודש נכנסה לבניין של נועה דרת רחוב, דפקה על דלתות הדיירים וצעקה. במקרה אחר, היא מספרת, אדם שהסתובב עם מסור ניסה לפרוץ לדירות. "יש לנו שומרים בבניין ואני אמורה להרגיש אקסטרה מוגנת, אבל זה כבר לא מרגיש מוגן", היא אומרת. "יש לי עכשיו תינוקת בת חודש וחצי, בבניין יש מלא ילדים קטנים, וזה נורא מלחיץ. אני לא ארד בערב עם העגלה והילדה להסתובב, מרגיש פה הארלם".
9	עדי שגרה במתחם נגה ביפו: זו בעיה שהולכת ומחריפה. אני גרה פה כבר חמש שנים ובשנה האחרונה זה נהיה פשוט קטסטרופה. אפילו בהליכה מהבית עד האוטו אפשר לראות שני חבר'ה עם מזרקים ביד על הרצפה ועל הספסל. וזה רק במרחק של שני מטר
10	התופעות של דרות רחוב ושימוש בסמים במרחב הציבורי מזוהות במשך שנים עם אזור התחנה המרכזית הישנה וכמה משכונות דרום תל אביב, שסובלות מהזנחה קשה והיעדר נוכחות משטרתית הולמת למה שמתרחש בהן. אלא שכעת, בשכונות נוספות בעיר מורגשת מציאות דומה. מכיכר דיזנגוף ועד שכונת מונטיפיורי, מתחם נוגה ביפו והרחובות הסמוכים לרוטשילד, מספרים תושבים על מפגעים תברואתיים ועל תחושת חוסר ביטחון שהולכת וגוברת. 
11	נועה מתגוררת בתל אביב כבר עשור, אבל לדבריה, השנה האחרונה הייתה שונה מכל מה שהכירה. "אני מרגישה שיש החמרה", היא אומרת. "ברוטשילד פעם היה נעים, היום זה כבר ממש לא המצב. אני לא אסתובב לבד באזור הבית שלי בערב אף פעם. אני אבקש ליווי מבעלי או אסע עם האוטו". 
12	לדבריה, המראות אינם מוגבלים לסביבת הבניין שלה. "אתמול הייתי אצל רופא בבוקר במרכז תל אביב, ובדרך לשם ראיתי כמות מטורפת של דרי רחוב ונרקומנים", היא אומרת. "ליד קניון גינדי אנשים שוכבים על הרצפה, זאת מכה. זה מרגיש כמו ניו יורק אחרי הקורונה. אני לא זוכרת שזה היה לי אף פעם בשום דירה שגרתי בה בעיר". לטענתה, גם המענה העירוני אינו מספק: "אני לא רואה אצלי אף פעם ניידות סיור של העירייה, וגם כשאנחנו קוראים למוקד לוקח להם הרבה זמן להגיע". 
13	המסקנה שלה עגומה. "אני מרגישה שאני מקבלת סימנים שאי אפשר לגור בתל אביב עם ילדים, כאילו העיר מגרשת אותנו", היא אומרת.
14	"אי אפשר לתאר את הריחות"
15	במתחם נוגה ביפו, עדי, שמתגוררת באזור כבר חמש שנים, מתארת מציאות שהפכה לדבריה לקשה במיוחד בשנה האחרונה. לטענתה, חלק מהבעיה קשור לפעילותו של גגון לדרי רחוב ביפו, שלדבריה פועל בשעות הערב והלילה בלבד, ומותיר את השוהים בו ללא מסגרת בשעות היום. "בבוקר הם יוצאים מהגגון ומסתובבים בשכונה. זה אומר שהם צריכים להיות איפשהו במהלך היום", היא מספרת. "האיפשהו הזה הוא בחדרי המדרגות שלנו, בתחנת הרכבת הקלה של סלמה, איפה שהם מצליחים לשבת. מדובר בבני אדם, אלה לא עכברים של אתר בנייה. אין להם איפה לעשות צרכים במהלך היום, אז הם פשוט עושים אותם באמצע הרחוב או בחדרי המדרגות של הבניינים שאנחנו גרים בהם".
16	באחד המקרים נאלצו דיירי הבניין להזעיק את מוקד 106 לאחר שדר רחוב ישן בפתח הבניין וחסם את הכניסה. "עשו לנו צרכים בכניסה לבניין, אי אפשר לתאר את הריחות", היא אומרת. "זו בעיה שהולכת ומחריפה. אני גרה פה כבר חמש שנים ובשנה האחרונה זה נהיה פשוט קטסטרופה. אפילו בהליכה מהבית עד האוטו אפשר לראות שני חבר'ה עם מזרקים ביד על הרצפה ועל הספסל. וזה רק במרחק של שני מטר".
17	עדי מתארת גם צעקות, הטרדות של יושבי בתי קפה וניסיונות פריצה למכוניות, שלדבריה מתרחשים בשכונה. "הרחובות מלוכלכים, מסריחים, לא בטוחים", היא אומרת. "אני כבר לא יוצאת לבד מהבית בערב".
18	אלא שבניגוד לקריאה להרחיק את דרי הרחוב מהשכונה, עדי מדגישה כי הפתרון חייב לתת מענה גם למצוקתם. לדבריה, העירייה הציבה סיירים שמסתובבים באזור, אך פעילותם אינה משנה את המציאות אלא רק מעבירה את האנשים ממקום למקום. "אם יושבים חמישה חבר'ה ועושים סמים בשדרות ירושלים, אז הם זזים למדרחוב אחר, ואחרי רבע שעה יזיזו אותם בחזרה לשדרות ירושלים וחוזר חלילה", היא מתארת. "משחקים איתם חתול ועכבר במקום למצוא פתרון. פתרון הומני גם כלפי התושבים וגם כלפי דרי הרחוב".
19	לטענתה, פניותיה לגורמים בעירייה לא זכו למענה. "פניתי לאנשים שונים בעירייה והם פשוט מתעלמים. מה שנוח לא להתעסק בו, לא מתעסקים. אין תגובה. זה מעליב, תגיבו". עדי גם מותחת ביקורת על סדרי העדיפויות העירוניים: "העירייה מתייחסת לנוגה כאל אזור יוקרה. אם כל צהלה הייתה מלאה בדרי רחוב הייתי מבינה את מחירי הארנונה וההתייחסות, אבל זאת לא צהלה. זאת יפו. יפו לא מקבלת משאבים מהעירייה נקודה".
20	"השינוי - מאז המלחמה"
21	גם במרכז תל אביב, באזור כיכר דיזנגוף, תושבות ותיקות מתארות שינוי. יובל בן גל (30), בעלת סטודיו לכושר שמתגוררת ברחוב סירקין, מספרת כי בשבוע האחרון נתקלה בכמה אירועים חריגים בסביבת ביתה. "ביום שבת בבוקר בשעה 11:00 חזרתי מטיול עם הכלב וראיתי נרקומן מנסה לפרק אופניים חשמליים מחוץ לבניין", היא מספרת. "יום אחרי, בדרך לאוטובוס, ראיתי הומלסים זרוקים בכל מקום. כל החברות שלי מדברות על זה". 
22	לדבריה, גם כיכר דיזנגוף עצמה הפכה למוקד של שימוש בסמים במרחב הציבורי. "נרקומנים מזריקים שם בשישי בערב", היא מספרת. במקרה אחר, היא מתארת אישה שעמדה באזור, צעקה ותלתה שלטים שמזמינים עוברי אורח לקיים יחסי מין איתה ועם כלב, תמורת תשלום. לדבריה, פקחים שהגיעו למקום לקחו את הכלב, אך היא אינה יודעת כיצד הסתיים הטיפול באירוע.
23	יובל מספרת כי גם מחוץ לסטודיו שלה ישנים דרי רחוב באופן קבוע. לתחושתה, מדובר בשינוי משמעותי לעומת השנים הקודמות. "משהו השתנה בשנה האחרונה, זה אף פעם לא היה ככה, ואני גרה פה כבר שבע שנים", היא אומרת.
24	נעמה, שגדלה באזור כיכר דיזנגוף ומתגוררת בו גם כיום, מתארת תחושה דומה. לדבריה, חלק מהתופעות באזור מוכרות לה עוד מילדותה, ובהן מקום שלטענתה משמש לזנות ברחוב בוגרשוב, אך בשנים האחרונות היא מבחינה בשינוי נוסף. "מאז המלחמה יש ממש שינוי, אני רואה יותר נרקומנים בלילה", היא מספרת.
25	תל אביב, יש לציין, אינה ייחודית. דרי רחוב נמשכים לערים גדולות כמו תל אביב וניו יורק בעיקר בשל הנגישות הגבוהה למשאבים חיוניים, שירותי רווחה והזדמנויות הישרדות שקשה למצוא ביישובים קטנים יותר; בראש ובראשונה, המטרופולינים מציעים רשת רחבה של מקלטים, בתי תמחוי וארגוני סיוע שמספקים מענה בסיסי לצורכיהם היומיומיים. בנוסף, צפיפות האוכלוסין והתנועה הערה של הולכי רגל ותיירים מגדילות משמעותית את האפשרויות לקיבוץ נדבות או לאיסוף בקבוקים וחפצים למיחזור, שמהווים מקור הכנסה מרכזי, וגם הגישה לסמים זמינה וקלה יותר.
26	מעבר לכך, הערים הגדולות מתאפיינות במערכות תחבורה ציבורית מפותחות שמאפשרות התניידות קלה ללא רכב. אופיין ההומה של הערים הללו מעניק מידה רבה של אנונימיות שמאפשרת לאותם אנשים להיטמע בנוף העירוני ולהימנע מהסטיגמה והביקורת החברתית שאופייניות לקהילות קטנות וסגורות.
27	תגובות
28	מעיריית תל אביב נמסר: "הביטחון האישי במרחב הציבורי ואכיפת עבירות פליליות, ובהן עבירות סמים, הן בראש ובראשונה באחריות משטרת ישראל. לצד זאת, העירייה פועלת באופן שוטף לצמצום מפגעים במרחב הציבורי, להגברת הנוכחות בשטח ולמתן מענה לתושבים ולדרי הרחוב. בחודשים האחרונים הוקמה באגף סל”ע יחידה ייעודית לשוהי רחוב בשיתוף מינהל השירותים החברתיים, המבצעת סיורים יזומים, מטפלת בפניות תושבים ומקדמת מענים טיפוליים ושיקומיים. בשנת 2025 טופלו באמצעות היחידה העירונית לדרי רחוב 1,263 אנשים במצבי רחוב, ובמקביל נרשם גידול של כ-300% בהפניות לבדיקות פסיכיאטריות כפויות במקרים המחייבים זאת.
29	"בניגוד לטענה כי אין מענה בשעות היום, בחודש יוני החל לפעול בגגון ביפו מרכז יום חדש לדרי רחוב, בנוסף לפעילות השוטפת של הגגון. באשר לפניות התושבים, העירייה פועלת לשיפור זמינות המענה, להגברת הנוכחות בשטח ולטיפול ממוקד במוקדים שבהם מתקבלות תלונות חוזרות. העירייה תמשיך לפעול, בשיתוף גורמי האכיפה והרווחה, לצמצום מפגעים במרחב הציבורי, לחיזוק תחושת הביטחון ולהרחבת המענים לאנשים במצבי רחוב ומצוקה".
30	לפי נתוני עיריית תל אביב-יפו, בשנת 2026 התקבלו 1,825 פניות במוקד 106 בנושאים שקשורים לדרי רחוב בצפון יפו, שכונת מונטיפיורי והחלק הדרומי של הצפון הישן. בצפון הישן התקבלו 941 פניות, כאשר הנושאים המרכזיים היו אלימות מצד דרי רחוב ופלישה לשטח ציבורי. בנוסף, התקבלו 187 פניות בנושא שימוש בסמים ומפגעים הקשורים לכך, וכן 653 פניות בנושאי רעש והפרעות במרחב הציבורי. באזור תיאטרון נוגה נפתחו מתחילת השנה 47 פניות שירות, וכולן טופלו ונסגרו.
31	מהמשטרה נמסר: "הטיפול בנושא דרי רחוב נמצא בסמכות ובאחריות הרשויות המקומיות, יחד עם זאת, משטרת ישראל פועלת בשיתוף פעולה הדוק עם הרשויות המקומיות, להגברת הנוכחות ותחושת הביטחון של התושבים. בנוגע לטיפול באירועים פלילים, קיימת עלייה משמעותית בפענוחי תיקים והגשת כתבי אישום בתחומי מחוז ת"א. לראייה, בהשוואה לתקופה מקבילה אשתקד נרשמה עלייה של כ-36% בכתבי האישום בעבירות הסחר בסמים וכ-6% בהגשת כתבי אישום בעבירות הרכוש, כל זאת כפועל יוצא מריבוי מעצרים איכותיים ופעילות אפקטיבית של הכוחות בשטח נגד  עבירות סחר בסמים ועבירות הרכוש".
32

8	The Trump administration is lifting some of its 50% tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterm elections, after a Republican candidate in a key US Senate race said she had lobbied for the change.
9	From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on products including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment", the White House said on Friday.
10	Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race to keep her seat in Maine, first announced the exemptions, saying they would help her state's agriculture industry.
11	The US imposed a 50% levy on $20bn (£15bn) worth of Canadian goods after trade talks between the two countries collapsed in August.
12	Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures in response to the US tariffs, which Prime Minister Mark Carney said were "necessary to protect our workers".
13	Last month, Carney matched the US tariffs "dollar for dollar" after the breakdown in talks. Trump had imposed them for what he called "unequal treatment" of US car, dairy and alcohol exports.
14	The White House said that, while tariffs would be lifted from some items, including some packing crates and boxes, they would be introduced on other items such as carpets and "waste products".
15	It said the action reflected US President Donald Trump's "continued efforts to defend American workers and ensure fair trade".
16	Trump "continues to address Canada's discriminatory treatment of US commerce", White House spokesman Matthew Middleton said.
17	Canada's internal trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said: "While we assess these latest steps, Canada stands ready to work constructively and in good faith towards a more mutually beneficial trading relationship that respects Canada's interests."
18	The White House's announcement comes less than a fortnight before the US midterm elections, which will determine whether Trump's Republican Party or Democrats will control Congress, impacting the remaining two years of his term.
19	Collins said she had repeatedly asked senior Trump officials for tariff relief and that she would "continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbour, ally and largest trading partner".
20	She wrote on X that the tariff exemptions were on products that were "crucial to Maine's agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers".
21	Collins' Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson, responded: "Trump's trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers. Susan Collins enabled this chaos, voted to confirm the people behind it and now wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire."
22	Maine borders the Canadian provinces New Brunswick and Quebec. Its economy, as well as that of other border states, is deeply linked to Canada and they have felt the effects of the months-long trade war.
23	Michigan lawmaker Mike Rogers, also a Republican, has called on Trump to end the standoff after spending months supporting the policy in recent advertisements airing in his trade-reliant state.
24	Also on Friday, Trump said Canada was "working very hard" on a trade deal with the US.
25	Carney, who has sought closer ties with Europe since the tariff war erupted, said that Canada was open to a mutually beneficial deal, but was willing to wait it out.
26	"We could sign it this afternoon if the US were there," he said on Friday, according to Canadian broadcaster CBC. "If it has to be months from now or longer than that, or another administration, before a proper deal comes into place, we will do that."
27	LeBlanc confirmed on Thursday that a delegation met members of the Canada-United States Economic Relations Advisory Committee - the ninth meeting since April 2026. The committee members discussed the ongoing impact of US tariffs in Canada.

8	In the sprawling former industrial city of Osasco, shuttered factories have given way to a shopping malls and delivery app tech companies in what is now dubbed São Paulo's "Silicon Valley."

---
name: fact-check
description: Independent verification of a drafted issue against the day's news bundle before publication. Use as the verifier subagent — given only the draft, its sources file and the bundle, check every claim and every rule, and return verdicts. Never used by the agent that wrote the draft.
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Glob, Grep
---

# The verifier

You check a drafted issue that someone else wrote. You did not see how it was written and you do
not trust it. Your job is to stop anything false, unsupported or manipulative from being published.

Read `.claude/skills/editor/SKILL.md` and `newspaper.toml` first: they define what the issue must
satisfy. Then read the draft (`issues/YYYY/MM/DD.md`) and its sources (`issues/YYYY/MM/DD.sources.json`).

## The evidence is the bundle

Every source in `sources.json` points to a bundle file, `work/YYYY-MM-DD/text/<id>.txt`. Those files
are the only evidence. You have no web access, and you need none: open the files.

## Check every claim

For each factual statement in the draft (every number, date, name, place, decision, attribution):

1. Find it in `sources.json`. A statement with no entry is **unsupported**.
2. Open the text file for its id. Confirm the quote is there and that it says what the draft says,
   in context: the right event, the right number, the right attribution, not something the article
   reports as a claim or a denial. Read around the quote, not only the quote.
3. Check the article's `Published` date in the file header. Old background stated as today's news
   is a **fix**.
4. Independence: the item needs one official primary source, or two independent outlets, as the
   editor skill says. Two outlets rewriting the same wire story count as one; look at their wording.
   A file marked "feed summary only" supports only what the summary itself says.
5. Give each statement a verdict:
   - **verified** — supported as written.
   - **fix** — supported, but the wording, number or attribution is off. Give the exact correction.
   - **unsupported** — no adequate evidence. Remove it; if the item no longer stands, remove the item.
   - **contradicted** — the files say otherwise. Remove it, or give both figures with attribution
     when reliable sources disagree.

Also check the frontmatter: weekday and Hebrew date for the date, and `number` one more than the
previous issue's. The calendar and on-this-day sections are claims like any other.

## Check every rule

Against the editor skill, flag: rhetoric presented as news, anonymous sourcing, allegations outside
a legal proceeding, numbers without context, adjectives of intensity, headlines that are not plain
declarative facts, sentences copied from a source, quotes longer than ten words in the issue text,
missing source lines, links in the body, and excluded topics. For the analysis piece, check the
fixed structure and that it takes no political side and makes no prediction.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Quality gate for an issue. The daily workflow publishes the issue only if this passes.

Checks: the issue parses; date and number are right; at least issue.publish_floor news items;
the verifier's report exists and did not FAIL; every news item has at least one source entry;
every quote in sources.json appears in its bundle file; no links in the issue text; run notes exist.

Usage: python3 scripts/check_issue.py YYYY-MM-DD
Exit 0 = publishable. Exit 1 = not; the problems are printed one per line.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
import unicodedata
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import build  # noqa: E402  (parser and config)


def norm(s: str) -> str:
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s)
    s = re.sub(r"[‘’‚‛′׳`´]", "'", s)
    s = re.sub(r"[“”„‟″״«»]", '"', s)
    s = re.sub(r"[‐-―−־]", "-", s)
    s = s.replace(" ", " ").replace("‏", "").replace("‎", "")
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip().casefold()


def main() -> None:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    day = date.fromisoformat(sys.argv[1])
    base = ROOT / "issues" / f"{day:%Y}" / f"{day:%m}" / f"{day:%d}"
    bundle = ROOT / "work" / day.isoformat() / "text"
    problems: list[str] = []
    cfg = build.CONFIG

    md = base.with_suffix(".md")
    if not md.exists():
        sys.exit(f"FAIL: {md.relative_to(ROOT)} does not exist")
    try:
        issue = build.parse_issue(md)
    except SystemExit as e:
        sys.exit(f"FAIL: issue does not parse: {e}")

    if str(issue.meta["date"]) != day.isoformat():
        problems.append(f"frontmatter date {issue.meta['date']} != {day}")
    previous = [i for i in build.load_issues() if i.day < day]
    want = int(previous[-1].meta["number"]) + 1 if previous else 1
    if str(issue.meta["number"]) != str(want):
        problems.append(f"number is {issue.meta['number']}, expected {want}")

    items = [it for s in issue.sections if s.kind == "desk" for it in s.items]
    floor = cfg["issue"].get("publish_floor", 5)
    if len(items) < floor:
        problems.append(f"only {len(items)} news items; publish_floor is {floor}")

    body = md.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if re.search(r"https?://|www\.", body):
        problems.append("the issue text contains a link; links are not allowed")

    check = base.with_suffix(".check.md")
    if not check.exists():
        problems.append("no verifier report (DD.check.md)")
    else:
        m = re.search(r"^Result:\s*(.+)$", check.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.M)
        if not m:
            problems.append("verifier report has no 'Result:' line")
        elif m.group(1).strip().upper().startswith("FAIL"):
            problems.append(f"verifier result is {m.group(1).strip()}")

    src_path = base.with_suffix(".sources.json")
    try:
        sources = json.loads(src_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except FileNotFoundError:

7	As France braces for new protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warned that calls for violence and looting were circulating online and pledged to deploy 70,000 police officers to secure order across the country.
8	"We will be uncompromising with rioters, looters and all those who commit acts of violence," Nunez told reporters on Friday.
9	The regular police officers will be reinforced by elite units, mounted police and heavy vehicles, and also equipped with helicopters, water cannon, drones and anti-drone systems, according to the minister.
10	"We will be extremely vigilant," he added, vowing to "let absolutely nothing pass."
11	Paris storekeepers prepare for more looting
12	The apparent show of force comes a week after riots ripped through Paris and other major cities.
13	While the ongoing political standoff started with students demanding better facilities, more teachers, and other improvements to the country's education system, it has grown into a general outpouring of anger over the cost of living.
14	Last Saturday, the protests escalated into violent riots, with authorities accusing radical militants and bands of young looters of taking advantage of the protesters' anger to sow chaos.
15	Police have faced groups of masked looters burning cars and buildings. Thousands of stores were ransacked.
16	Addressing reporters on Friday, the interior minister said that the unrest was "completely unacceptable" and said the authorities "will do everything in our power" to avoid a repeat of the violence.
17	Meanwhile, Paris shopkeepers were seen boarding up their windows. The city council called on residents and business owners to remove objects that could be set on fire or used as either projectiles or barricades.
18	Who will be marching on Saturday?
19	Nunez also said authorities will maintain curfews in designated areas of the city. This will include restrictions between 11 pm and 6 am in two central Paris squares, according to the local police.
20	The police approved only one protest march, organized by labor union CGT, on a limited route through Paris on Saturday. The authorities rejected requests by France's biggest student union UNEF and its anti-establishment Yellow Vest movement to hold their own rallies.
21	However, UNEF pledged to go ahead with its protest regardless, while Yellow Vest supporters were expected to join the official march.
22	Authorities had banned all protests in France's second largest city, Marseille, before walking the decision back and allowing a union demonstration. Authorities also intend to keep protesters away from the center of Lyon, France's third most populous city.
23	Students 'not satisfied' after meeting Macron
24	The government, led by centrist President Emmanuel Macron, sought to differentiate between what they see as legitimate protests and the violent unrest.
25	Macron himself also dismissed the narrative that Islamist extremists and migrants were driving the violence. He has, however, pointed to far-left groups and accused them of trying to stage a coup.
26	On Friday, Macron also held his first-ever meeting with representatives of secondary school students. However, the meeting ended with the pupils calling for more protests.
27	"We are not satisfied," said student representative Nathanael Combary, president of campaign group High School Renewal.
28	He told reporters that the president had been "attentive" but that the students were still waiting for concrete proposals to be presented at their meeting with the prime minister on Monday.
29	He urged his fellow students to "continue to mobilize" and maintain a "standoff" with the government.

A sense of hope swept through Belgrade on Thursday evening as thousands gathered for the final rally of the Student List, the group of candidates put forward by the student movement that has been protesting against the government for almost exactly two years.
The Student List is calling for an end to the current regime in Serbia via the ballot box in Sunday's parliamentary election.
Many of those who attended the rally had spent days walking to the Serbian capital from all four corners of the country, turning the campaign finale into a display of solidarity and peaceful determination.
"We have walked across Serbia from one end to the other, visited villages and neighborhoods, looked you in the eye and realized that we can count on you," biology student Arsa Stojanovic told the crowd.
"People, it smells like freedom," added Aleksandar Cupic, professor of transport and traffic engineering, and a candidate on the Student List.
Students emerge as agents of change
After 24 months of protests sparked by the collapse of a concrete canopy at Novi Sad railway station, which killed 16 people in November 2024, Serbia is heading into an election unlike any other in the 14 years since the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) first came to power.
For the first time in years, the ruling party faces a serious political challenge, which this time comes from a student movement that has channeled widespread public discontent into an electoral campaign.

Source: The Guardian World
Title: Oil price rises above $117 a barrel amid fears US will renew strikes on Iran
URL: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/23/oil-five-month-high-fears-us-renews-strikes-iran
Published: 2026-10-23T16:48:28+00:00
Content: full article text

Oil has hit its highest level in more than six months as fears of fresh escalation in the Middle East conflict grip the energy markets.
Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, rose by about 3.5% on Friday to pass $117 a barrel at one point – its highest level since April.
The jump came after Tehran said it would attack oil facilities, undersea cables, datacentres and AI facilities in the Gulf region if a new US-Israeli offensive was launched against Iran.
Richard Hunter, of the broker Interactive Investor, said: “Widespread reports that the US is considering renewed military strikes on Iran after the midterm elections rather than pursuing a diplomatic route was enough for the price to pop, after what many had considered would be a brief conflict is now in its eighth month.”
The oil price later eased back slight to sit about 2.7% up at just over $116 a barrel. Brent crude had traded at about $72 a barrel back in February, before the Iran war began, but soared to touch $126 a barrel by the end of April.
Tensions in the region have been rising this week and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed to have struck four commercial ships in the strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. The US state department ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia, which has faced continued attacks from Houthi rebels in Yemen.
Susannah Streeter, the chief investment strategist at the broker Wealth Club, said fears were rising that American and Israeli forces would be ordered to launch strikes on Iran’s energy infrastructure after the US elections on 3 November.
She added: “At the same time, the attacks on Saudi Arabia’s facilities by Houthi rebels have intensified this week, and for ships attempting to cross the strait of Hormuz, it’s still a dangerous journey, with projectiles still being fired.”
Streeter said Ukraine’s bombardment of Russian diesel refineries was also adding to supply concerns.
----
Source: Ars Technica
Title: Moderna and Merck say their mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42%
URL: https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/10/personalized-mrna-cancer-vaccine-cut-melanoma-death-recurrence-by-42/
Published: 2026-10-22T22:12:19+00:00
Content: full article text

Personalized mRNA vaccines against melanoma—the deadliest form of skin cancer—reduced the risk of death or recurrence by 42 percent compared to standard treatment in a late-stage trial, pharmaceutical partners Merck and Moderna announced Thursday.
The results are a significant advance in melanoma treatment; Merck and Moderna are already engaging with regulatory authorities to get the vaccine approved. More broadly, the vaccine’s success bolsters hope that mRNA vaccines and individualized cancer-targeting medicines offer a new paradigm for cancer therapies.
“From the beginning, we believed mRNA technology could make it possible to develop cancer treatments uniquely matched to each patient’s tumor,” Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel said in a statement. The trial results “mark a defining moment for that vision and show what’s possible when we rethink how medicines are made.” They also “reinforce our conviction that mRNA has the potential to fundamentally change how we treat cancer,” he said.
In August, Moderna and Merck reported that the vaccine has succeeded in the trial, but held off reporting details until the data could be presented at an upcoming scientific conference. That conference is the European Society of Medical Oncology, starting now in Madrid, Spain. The data was scheduled for presentation on Saturday, but after an oncology news site reported the results early, breaking the embargo, the companies released the top-line results. The full data has been accepted for publication in the New England Journal of Medicine.
As Ars reported earlier, the Phase 3 trial included 1,137 patients who had stage IIB–IV melanoma that had been surgically removed prior to entering the trial. Patients were randomized 2-1 to receive either a combination treatment including the personalized mRNA vaccine with a standard treatment, or the standard treatment alone. The standard treatment was Merck’s established monoclonal antibody cancer treatment Keytruda.

For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet.
It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert.
Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side programming language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks.
Governments and cyber-security agencies rushed to contain the fallout, urging website owners to check if their sites were affected and, if so, install updates to patch the issue or consider going offline.
There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far.
But in the days since the issues came to light, disruption to sites and services has continued to ripple around the world.
What is PHP?
Most people may not have heard of PHP, but they probably interact with it daily.
It stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, an open-source, back-end programming language which runs on a web server.
Developed in the early 1990s to help serve dynamic web pages and applications, PHP still powers lots of platforms today, including Wikipedia, online shops and WordPress – the system behind many websites.
When you visit a site, PHP is the code which collects data and effectively turns it into a page you can read.
It has also been used to write a number of tools for building or speeding up the creation of web apps, with Laravel, Symfony and Drupal among popular PHP frameworks.
According to cyber-security firm Wiz, which helped uncover the critical PHP vulnerabilities surfaced this week, PHP powers 70% of the world's websites.
It is maintained by a non-profit called the PHP Foundation, external, composed of individuals and companies which depend on the language and aim to ensure its "long-term prosperity".
What is the vulnerability?
A group of cyber-security researchers and organisations disclosed two vulnerabilities within PHP this week, which they warned could have the potential to upend sites across the internet.
Cyber firms Wiz and Calif said the flaws were inherent in the language itself, affecting versions of PHP released over the last decade.
The technical bugs, given the technical IDs CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were ranked a 9.2 out of 10 in severity by researchers.
Calif researcher Ryan Austin, who helped uncover it, told the BBC it was "the most serious vulnerability I've ever found".
Wiz wrote in a blog post, external about its findings that, under the right conditions, hackers could exploit the bugs to take control of affected web servers and steal sensitive data - saying everything built on PHP was left exposed.
AI could also make such attacks easier and faster, Paul Spain, chief executive of Gorilla Cyber Security, told the BBC.
He estimated the flaw could affect "millions and millions" of websites.
Jill Slay, a cyber-security researcher at the University of Adelaide, said it would be "disastrous" if hackers or countries weaponised the flaw and seized private data from websites.

Hacking attempts rise after flaws found in program affecting 70% of websites
A few months ago AI caused global alarm after autonomous agents were found to have cheated on evaluations and then tried to cover it up, in what became known as the "Hugging Face hack."
This week, AI and hacking are back in the spotlight with AI technology credited to have helped prevent a global cybersecurity crisis.
Cybersecurity firm Wiz Research, using OpenAI technology, announced on Wednesday it had discovered security flaws in a computer programming language that helps run some 70% of the world's websites.
OpenAI called the bug "one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory." Wiz Research warned that its "successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them."
Corporations and governments from the U.K. to Japan are now rushing to prevent hackers from capitalizing on the flaws.
The flaws were discovered in a major programming language called PHP, short for Hypertext Preprocessor. Wiz Research calls PHP "the backbone of the web," saying the technology has underpinned much of the internet since the 1990s.
"These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history," the firm said, adding that before publicly disclosing the flaw, teams had worked on building a solution that's now available to websites to protect themselves.
As countries scrambled to prevent cyberattacks, numerous websites and pages were taken offline in the past few days. The U.S. National Security Agency warned organizations using PHP to "maintain heightened awareness" over the coming weeks. The U.K.'s National Cyber Security Center called on organizations to "take immediate action" to update their websites to the latest fixed or patched version.
Dozens of British and Finnish government services were taken offline this week. In France, many local government sites were also briefly taken down. China's Industry Ministry urged entities to review security gaps.
In Japan, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi put out "an urgent request for everyone to take action," adding, "If it is difficult to apply the fix patch promptly, temporarily suspending websites and similar measures can be considered an effective way to reduce risk."
Matthew Prince, the head of the cybersecurity firm Cloudflare, said his organization saw tens of thousands of attempts to exploit the flaw in the first 45 minutes of its discovery. That's now in the millions, Prince said on Thursday.
Wiz Research said the flaws in PHP had been present for decades.

Cybersecurity teams around the globe are rushing to patch PHP programming language flaws this week, in an artificial intelligence safety moment that's being described as "Black October."
Nearly 70% of all websites use PHP, according to some estimates.
"In the last 2 days there have been several dozen cyber attacks which, in isolation, would each have been the worst to happen in an entire calendar year," John Milinovich, senior director of product management at Figma, wrote in a post on X on Thursday. "Every sector from government to education to big tech and banks is being massively affected, and people are starting to freak out."
Researchers at Google's Wiz and the AI firm Calif discovered major vulnerabilities in PHP in August by using advanced AI models from OpenAI and Google. But by Tuesday, the warnings had spread online, prompting governments and businesses around the globe to scramble to contain the fallout.
Major AI companies have been warning about the technology's advancing cybersecurity capabilities since April, when Anthropic announced a limited rollout of its powerful model called Mythos. Concerns mounted in July, when OpenAI disclosed that two of its models escaped containment, accessed the open internet and breached a company called Hugging Face.
Experts believe the PHP security flaws serve as the latest example of what's to come.
Jason Clinton, deputy chief information security officer at Anthropic, wrote in a post on X on Thursday that the cybersecurity landscape is likely to get "a lot worse" before it gets better.
"Security leaders, never let a crisis go to waste: please go to your boards and ask for help right now," Clinton said. "Not for ai, for the basics. (we need to hold on for ~18 months.)"
While many large companies have access to advanced models that they can use to harden their systems, serious bugs could be more challenging for small- and medium-sized businesses to address, Chris Krebs, former director of the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, told CNBC on Friday. He encouraged smaller companies to "constantly" scan for vulnerabilities, deploy patches as fast as possible or take legacy systems offline.
"This is a significant week or two in cybersecurity," Krebs told CNBC's "Squawk Box." "As I mentioned, 3% of all critical vulnerabilities ever discovered have been found in the last month."
Figma's Milinovich encouraged individuals to set up two-factor authentication for "everything," use a password manager, set up an identity protection app and move smart devices to their own network. He added that people should lean in and experiment with AI to understand how powerful the tools have become.

Source: The Guardian Science
Title: ‘Bespoke’ mRNA vaccine significantly reduces risk of melanoma recurrence or death, clinical trial shows
URL: https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/oct/23/mrna-vaccine-melanoma-cancer-breakthrough-australia
Published: 2026-10-23T04:27:18+00:00
Content: full article text

A personalised mRNA-based melanoma vaccine significantly reduces the risk of cancer recurrence or death within two years, new clinical trial results show.
The vaccine, intismeran, is custom-made to target genetic mutations unique to an individual’s melanoma. It is the first individualised cancer vaccine to show positive results in a phase III clinical trial.
The Australian-led trial included 1,137 patients whose melanoma had been surgically removed but were at high risk of it returning.
All were treated with an immunotherapy drug called pembrolizumab for twelve months, and some were also given the personalised intismeran vaccine.
The trial found that at two years post treatment, the combination of intismeran and pembrolizumab reduced the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42% compared with treatment with pembrolizumab alone.
Prof Georgina Long, medical director at the Melanoma Institute Australia and 2024 Australian of the Year, described the findings as “a foundational shift in our approach to cancer”, allowing scientists to “harness … the immune system in a more personalised way to reduce the risk of melanoma recurrence or death. This has not been achieved before in the history of cancer drug development.”
Long will present the results at the European Society for Medical Oncology’s annual congress in Madrid on the weekend.
The results have been accepted for publication in the New England Journal of Medicine.
Patients in the trial – conducted across 157 sites worldwide – had not previously received any cancer drug treatment. Of those receiving the combination of intismeran and pembrolizumab, 82% were alive and recurrence-free after two years, compared with 70% of participants treated with pembrolizumab alone.
In a phase III trial, a treatment is tested in a large group of people and compared with standard treatments; it is necessary before drug regulators can approve a medicine for use in the general population.
In recent years, developments in immunotherapy drugs have significantly increased survival rates for people with advanced melanoma.
Dr Jessamy Tiffen, acting deputy director of the Centre for Cancer Innovations at the Centenary Institute, who was not involved in the research, said what was “truly remarkable” about the vaccine was the “deeply personalised nature of the treatment, something cancer researchers have been striving to achieve for decades”.
“Where previously oncologists could pick a targeted therapy based on a single gene mutation present in the melanoma, this bespoke mRNA vaccine targets up to 34 gene mutations, unique to each patient. This vaccine, in combination with another type of immunotherapy, then trains the immune system to recognise and eliminate the melanoma, and most importantly, stop it from coming back.”
She noted that the treatment, if progressed, would not benefit all people with melanoma. “A significant portion do not respond to the vaccine in the first instance,” she said.
“Cancer cells also have an insidious ability to adapt and evade whatever treatment we throw at them. Only time will tell how effective the treatment is beyond two years, but the results are clear that the combination works better than immunotherapy alone, and that’s a very exciting development.”
The drug manufacturers said it was too early to tell from the data whether the combination treatment improved long-term survival.
Prof Christopher Sweeney, director of the South Australian immunoGENomics Cancer Institute at Adelaide University, described the vaccine as “a step-change approach for how to improve the body’s immune system to see cancer cells as foreign and then augment the ability to prevent the cancer cells growing and recurring”.
He said more research was needed to see if the approach was effective in patients “who have cancer we can see”, or who were not responsive to the immune enhancer pembrolizumab.
The personalised vaccine will not be available as a standard melanoma treatment until it has gone through further study and regulatory review, a process that may take several years.
----
Source: NPR World
Title: Europe's heat claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
URL: https://www.npr.org/2026/10/23/g-s1-149498/europe-heat-deaths
Published: 2026-10-23T04:17:06-04:00
Content: full article text

Europe's heat claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
WASHINGTON — Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.
Researchers modeled heat-related deaths for different age groups in 854 European cities during repeated heat waves in June, July and August and found that 50,391 people died from warmer temperatures, and of those, 32,619 died because of the extra heat caused by the burning of coal, oil and gas, according to a study in an upcoming issue of Nature Health.
That's 71% higher than the previous deadliest summer, which was 29,480 in 2022, according to the same researchers, who produced a study earlier this month tracking yearly summer heat-related deaths in those European cities. And this summer's death figures are underestimates because they don't count a deadly heat wave in May and they only look at deaths in those 854 cities, which are about 40% of Europe's population, study authors said.
About one-third of the deaths were from June 17 to July 1, a particularly intense heat wave when temperatures were 9.5 degrees Fahrenheit (5.3 degrees Celsius) above normal, said study co-author Garyfallos Konstantinoudis, a biostatistician at Imperial College London.
"Much of Western and Northern Europe, our infrastructure is just not designed to cope with the sort of temperatures that we are seeing now because of the effects of human-caused warming," said lead author Clair Barnes, a climate scientist at Imperial College London. She said some European cities this summer had temperatures 21.6 F (12 C) warmer than normal.
Of those 50,000, more than 32,000 died from the added heat of human-caused climate change, the study also found. Italy, France, Spain and Germany had the highest death tolls, the study said. Of all the European capitals, Rome had the highest heat death total from 2000 to 2025, according to the team's study earlier this month.
An extra dose of heat from fossil fuel burning
This would've already been an abnormal natural hot spell on top of a huge amount of climate change, Barnes said. She said Europe is the fastest-warming continent — although the Arctic, which is not a continent, is warming even faster — and is 4.5 F (2.5 C) hotter than pre-industrial times.
"Just the underlying warming from human activity, from mostly the burning of fossil fuels, it's increasing all of our temperatures by what sounds like quite a small amount," Barnes said. "For many people, it's certainly the case that that extra two-and-a-half degrees (Celsius) of warming is what's going to tip those temperatures from uncomfortable to dangerous and potentially deadly."
More than half of the people who died in Europe's heat were age 85 or older, but the stifling temperatures also killed more than 800 people between the ages of 20 and 44, Konstantinoudis said.
How the death numbers are calculated
The team used an established and accepted scientific method to figure out how many of the 50,000 heat deaths were from natural high summer heat and how many were due to what heat-trapping gases have done to the climate. They ran computer simulations of a world without climate change and compared it to the deaths that happened this summer. The difference is what was caused by global warming.
The percentage of heat deaths attributable to global warming has grown from about 45% in the early 2000s to 65% now, Barnes said.
"Summers are getting hotter, and the analytical tools for attributing deaths to heat are getting more accurate," said Dr. Howard Frumkin, former director of the National Center for Environmental Health in the U.S., who wasn't part of the study. "Together, these two trends yield increasingly high and increasingly accurate counts of heat-related deaths."
The scientific team also had to use statistical modeling to come up with the base count of 50,000 heat deaths because those deaths are underreported and often not listed in death certificates, despite being a major factor, Konstantinoudis said. Several outside experts agreed with him, calling the methods state-of-the-art.
The researchers ran a complex mathematical equation that has been used in several previously peer-reviewed studies, Barnes said, which factors in specific age and temperatures for each of the 854 cities based on a localized optimal temperature that coincides with the fewest deaths. When it's warmer or colder, the equation calculates excess deaths above lowest-death conditions.
Researchers then checked their calculations against real-time estimates from government agencies. Mostly — but not always — they matched fairly well, Konstantinoudis said. The team's methods for May and June British heat waves calculated 2,700 excess deaths and the United Kingdom health statistics agency said it was 2,800, he said.
Cooling and adapting are needed, but they're not enough
"We need to prepare for the heat we cannot now avoid, with urgent investments in heat early-warning systems, equitable access to low-carbon cooling, and neighborhood buddy systems that check on and support people most at risk — while rapidly reducing the fossil fuel use driving the crisis," said Canadian emergency room physician Dr. Courtney Howard, president-elect of the Canadian Medical Association, who wasn't part of the research.
Adapting is only part of the answer, said Dr. Jonathan Patz of the University of Wisconsin-Madison, who wasn't part of the research but also praised it.
"We can't just be mopping up the mess on the floor without thinking about turning the faucet off," said Patz, a professor of health and the environment. "So we need prevention at different levels. We need better cooling and protecting vulnerable populations from inevitable increased frequency and extreme heat waves. But we also need to go to the root of the problem and absolutely address the burning of fossil fuels."
---
Source: Nature News

Title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c60qk573yzz8o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss
Published: 2026-10-24T00:36:47+00:00
Content: full article text

- Published
The Trump administration is lifting some of its 50% tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterm elections, after a Republican candidate in a key US Senate race said she had lobbied for the change.
From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on products including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment", the White House said on Friday.
Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race to keep her seat in Maine, first announced the exemptions, saying they would help her state's agriculture industry.
The US imposed a 50% levy on $20bn (£15bn) worth of Canadian goods after trade talks between the two countries collapsed in August.
Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures in response to the US tariffs, which Prime Minister Mark Carney said were "necessary to protect our workers".
Last month, Carney matched the US tariffs "dollar for dollar" after the breakdown in talks. Trump had imposed them for what he called "unequal treatment" of US car, dairy and alcohol exports.
The White House said that, while tariffs would be lifted from some items, including some packing crates and boxes, they would be introduced on other items such as carpets and "waste products".
It said the action reflected US President Donald Trump's "continued efforts to defend American workers and ensure fair trade".
Trump "continues to address Canada's discriminatory treatment of US commerce", White House spokesman Matthew Middleton said.
Canada's internal trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said: "While we assess these latest steps, Canada stands ready to work constructively and in good faith towards a more mutually beneficial trading relationship that respects Canada's interests."
The White House's announcement comes less than a fortnight before the US midterm elections, which will determine whether Trump's Republican Party or Democrats will control Congress, impacting the remaining two years of his term.
Collins said she had repeatedly asked senior Trump officials for tariff relief and that she would "continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbour, ally and largest trading partner".
She wrote on X that the tariff exemptions were on products that were "crucial to Maine's agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers".
Collins' Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson, responded: "Trump's trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers. Susan Collins enabled this chaos, voted to confirm the people behind it and now wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire."

Title: Trump dropping some Canada tariffs but 'replacing' them with other products
URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/trump-tariffs-canada-susan-collins.html
Published: 2026-10-23T21:26:59+00:00
Content: full article text

The White House on Friday said it would drop tariffs on some Canadian goods, but replace them with other products from the major U.S. trade partner.
The move was revealed after Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, took credit for pushing the Trump administration to issue tariff exemptions on several categories of Canadian imports she says are "crucial" for her state's industries.
But Collins' announcement, which The Wall Street Journal first reported, did not mention that while tariffs would be removed for some Canadian products, new ones would be added to the list of goods subject to steep U.S. duties. The White House announced the new tariffs less than an hour after Collins touted the new exemptions to the tariffs, which are unpopular in the state where she's fighting for reelection.
President Donald Trump earlier Friday signed a proclamation "removing certain products" from the list of items that he slapped 50% tariffs on over the summer using a 96-year-old trade law.
But he is "replacing those products with certain valves, carpets, waste products, and others," according to a White House fact sheet detailing the proclamation.
The changes are being made to "further refine the scope of the tariffs on certain Canadian products," according to the fact sheet, which does not mention Maine.
The new additions and removals from the list of goods covered by the "Section 338" tariffs will take effect Oct. 30, four days before the Nov. 3 U.S. election, the fact sheet said.
Asked what Collins had agreed to in her conversations pushing Trump administration officials for lower tariffs on products affecting her state, her spokeswoman Phoebe Keller told CNBC that the senator "requested exemptions for products that are important to Maine and will continue to do so."
Before the fact sheet was made public, Collins' office sent a press release crediting the senator with securing the new tariff exemptions on "nine categories of products crucial for Maine's agricultural industries."
That announcement came as voters have already started casting ballots in the pivotal Maine Senate race, where Trump's unpopular tariffs have been a top issue.

Despite downgrade consensus, the agency kept France's sovereign rating unchanged, a short-lived relief, say economists, warning of a debt time bomb and worsening political and social tensions.
An unexpected piece of good news: Moody's has left France's sovereign debt rating untouched. Although markets had widely expected a downgrade, the New York-based agency on Friday evening maintained its assessment at Aa3 with a negative outlook.
France's ten-year borrowing rate (OAT) has soared this week, while the country is under strain after the riots of 17 October, which have added to investor unease. Moody's nevertheless justified its stance in a statement, explaining that "the Aa3 rating is based on the assumption that a 2027 budget reducing the deficit will be adopted, while funding costs and social tensions will moderate somewhat over the coming months".
As soon as the announcement was made, the government rushed to hail the decision. Economy Minister Roland Lescure was the first to react. He sees in it "recognition of the strength of our economy and the credibility of the budget" presented by the government. In his view, the goal of adopting by the end of the year a "responsible" budget that brings the deficit down to 5% is "non-negotiable".
In a more defensive tone, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu welcomed on X the fact that Moody's decision "confounds the doom-laden forecasts of many 'experts'" (his quotation marks) "and of those who speculate on French debt".
According to the head of government, the ongoing budget debate in the National Assembly "shows our creditors that there is a way forward".
He also highlighted a measure which, in his view, reflects the seriousness of current economic policy: "With the release of 10 million barrels of diesel we will have an impact on pump prices from 1 November, without playing fast and loose with the public finances".

Title: OBS Studio 33
URL: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/releases/tag/33.0.0
Published: 2026-10-24T04:49:58Z
Content: full article text

33.0 New Features
- Updated CEF from 127/6533 to 150/7871 [WizardCM] (#13900)
  - This is a massive update to the underlying framework used for browser sources and docks from the July 2024 release to September 2026
  - All of this work is on the backend and should be invisible to users. Please be sure to report any new weirdness or problems you run into with browser sources!
- Complete overhaul to plugin loading [FiniteSingularity/PatTheMav] (#13594)
  - First-party plugins are now in a new folder named core
  - Third-party plugins have an updated installation location and folder structure
  - Existing third-party plugins will continue to load from the legacy locations until OBS Studio 34.0
  - More information is available in our knowledge base article
- Improved how source snapping works in the preview [Warchamp7] (#12298)
  - New visual indicator added
  - Sources now snap along the entire axis instead of only when directly touching
  - Sources no longer snap to hidden sources
- Improved behavior of spinboxes for number values [Warchamp7] (#12337)
  - Typing is no longer mysteriously blocked in some situations
  - Numbers are no longer cut off in some situations
  - Values now update only after pressing Enter and Enter does not close the window
  - Holding Shift + Up/Down now advances multiple steps at a time
  - Dragging the cursor inside the input but outside the text itself now works properly
- Enabled NVENC on Arm64 [RytoEX] (#13827)
33.0 Changes
- Added a check for encoders being missing when loading a profile [derrod] (#11340)
- Added support for newest NVIDIA Broadcast SDKs for NVIDIA Audio Effects and Video Effects [pkviet] (#13838)
- Added hotkeys for controlling audio monitoring of a source [Warchamp7] (#13599)
- Changed Safe Mode to not start WebSocket Server [FiniteSingularity/RytoEX] (#13984)
- Fixed issues with groups in Studio Mode [Warchamp7] (#11092)

Title: Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed
URL: https://www.kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro
Published: 2026-10-23T16:59:08Z
Content: full article text

Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
We're introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in our new K3.1 series and our most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window. It delivers substantial improvements across coding, 3D creation, financial research, and other agentic capabilities.
We are also releasing Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which delivers 2-3× the speed of K3.1 Pro for more responsive interactions.
Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed are available today on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API. The full model weights will be released by Nov 4.
Advancing the Frontier of Open Intelligence
Kimi K3.1 Pro is a post-trained version of Kimi K3, with substantially larger post-training compute. To enable large-scale joint RL across hundreds of downstream domains, we optimized every layer of the stack — the RL framework, long-context inference, training efficiency, sandbox infrastructure, rollout scheduling, and a shared platform for environment quality checks — so that each increment of RL compute delivers stable, predictable returns. As a result, K3.1 Pro achieves consistent gains in every domain.
Across coding, agentic, and knowledge benchmarks, K3.1 Pro matches or approaches the strongest proprietary models. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which evaluates coding agents on realistic, resource-constrained terminal tasks using strict task-specific tests, K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and narrowly behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%). And on Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon, our internal benchmark that tests coding agents' multi-step execution, tool use, and end-to-end problem solving across diverse engineering domains, K3.1 Pro scores 61.2%, above K3's 55.95%.
Coding
K3.1 Pro covers the full range of coding work, from quick fixes in real codebases to full-project builds. It also brings a more considered visual style to games and web experiences, and knows how to build them with the right tools.
K3.1 Pro works effectively across game engines such as Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot, combining them with web search and 3D generation to create complete experiences. Its front-end pages, interactive Three.js scenes, and 3D assets show stronger composition, typography, animation, and polish. The examples below were created end to end by K3.1 Pro:
K3.1 Pro's long-horizon coding capabilities are also strengthened through large-scale reinforcement learning. In one internal test, it built a human walking dynamics simulator with integrated training and evaluation pipelines on top of human-atlas, an open-source anatomical model of the human body comprising 296 skeletal components, including cartilage, and 402 muscle components. Eight people were killed on Friday when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan, in a rare attack on Jordan’s Christian minority that authorities described as a terrorist act by extremists.
Maj gen Abdallah al-Maaytah, the head of the country’s Public Security Directorate, said most of those injured in the shooting at St George’s Greek Orthodox church in Hamoud, in Karak governorate, were still receiving treatment, and that the hunt for the attackers was continuing. Such attacks are extremely rare in Jordan, which is relatively stable, though authorities in the US say that in recent years they have repeatedly foiled attempted attacks by Islamist militants.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility.

Twenty-seven of the injured are receiving hospital treatment.

The shooting occurred at the Hammoud Church and reportedly took place during a funeral.

A witness told Jordanian state media there were 150 to 200 people present at the church at the time of the shooting. Videos circulating online showed wounded people on the floor of the church covered in blood, but this footage cannot be verified by DW.
Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya said a group of "extremists" carried out the massacre. According to Jordanian outlet Roya News, Al-Faraya said authorities already possess the names of suspects behind the attacks but would not publicly disclose their identities as of now.
Jordanian government spokesperson Mohammad al-Momani said security forces have launched a probe into the attack.

Hasanenko estimated that around 2,000 people remained in Oleshky, including 35 children who, she said, were unable to leave.

US First Lady Melania Trump has secured an agreement between Russia and Ukraine to temporarily halt military operations in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, the White House announced on Friday. The intent is to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and evacuate civilians trapped near the front line.
The localised ceasefire is scheduled to begin on 29 October, with both sides agreeing to suspend military action in the southern Ukrainian city and establish a designated safe passage for residents wishing to leave, according to the White House.
Oleshky lies on the Russian-occupied eastern bank of the Dnipro River, opposite the Ukrainian-controlled city of Kherson. Before Russia's full-scale invasion, it had approximately 24,000 residents. According to White House estimates, only 1,700 to 2,000 remain, including around 50 children.
The announcement comes amid a deepening humanitarian crisis in Oleshky, where residents face severe shortages of food, clean water and medicine, while attempts to escape have exposed civilians to mines and drone attacks.

"The city is practically destroyed," she said. "There is almost no building that has not been damaged."
Hasanenko estimated that around 2,000 people remained in Oleshky, including 35 children who, she said, were unable to leave.

Search and rescue efforts continued after at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. It was the biggest quake in the region in the past five years, according to China’s national broadcaster CCTV.
More than 1,600 people from the local county were deployed to help rescue efforts. Supplies were also sent into the region, including 1,000 prefabricated housing units, about 3,000 tents, folding beds, torches and winter clothing.
The US Geological Survey said the quake occurred at 10.33pm local time on Thursday, with its epicentre 119 miles (191km) east-north-east of Nagqu, in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area of northern Tibet. It put the earthquake’s depth at 11 miles.
The agency recorded at least seven aftershocks of magnitudes between 4.3 and 5.2, all of them with a depth of 6 miles. Videos posted by CCTV showed workers running out of restaurants and objects falling off shelves at supermarkets when the quake struck.
China’s official Xinhua news agency said on Friday that communication in some areas hit by the quake was down. Local railway authorities had taken emergency actions to stop trains passing through the region.
More than 300 police officers were dispatched for relief work while the regional fire and rescue services had sent almost 350 personnel to the affected areas, Xinhua reported. Rescue workers clambered through damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs, footage on CCTV showed.
The earthquake caused rockfalls, forcing local authorities to close a section of national highway 317, allowing only emergency, rescue and official support vehicles through as crews worked to clear debris, according to Xinhua. Intermittent snow was expected in the region over the next three days, Xinhua said.
China’s president, Xi Jinping, called for an all-out effort in the rescue operation and medical relief work.
Nagqu is more than 185 miles north of Tibet’s capital, Lhasa. Earthquakes are relatively common in China. In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in one in Tibet’s rural Tingri county.
In August, a disastrous flood hit the border of Tibet and Nepal. China’s tight grip on information prevented international media from visiting the affected regions on the Tibetan side, obscuring the scale of the damage.
In December 2023, a quake in remote Gansu province in north-west China killed at least 134 people, state media said. That quake was China’s deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people died in the south-western province of Yunnan.
Tibet is a particularly seismically active area. The high-altitude region was taken under Chinese control in the 1950s and its people, who are predominantly ethnic Tibetans, have had a tense relationship with the authorities in Beijing since. As well as being one of the poorest regions in China, many Tibetans reject Beijing-imposed controls on their culture and religion.
Agence France-Presse contribute to this report

URL: https://www.walla.co.il/news/israel/383958603
Published: 2026-10-23T08:12:50+00:00
Content: full article text

פיאסקו סביבתי מתמשך במפרץ חיפה: ימים ספורים בלבד לאחר שהמשרד להגנת הסביבה התיר למפעל גדיב (מקבוצת בז"ן) לחדש את עבודות התחזוקה תחת מה שהוגדר כ"מנגנוני בקרה מחמירים", שוב נרשמה אמש (חמישי) חריגה חמורה מהתקן היממתי לחומר המסרטן בנזן בתחנת הניטור בקריית בנימין. בעקבות החריגה, הופסקה פעילות התחזוקה במפעל באופן מיידי על פי הוראות הצו המנהלי, ונכון להבוקר ירדו הריכוזים וחזרו לטווח התקן.
מדובר באירוע חריג במיוחד – שכן לפי איגוד ערים מפרץ חיפה להגנת הסביבה, חריגה יממתית מתקן הבנזן בתחנה זו לא נמדדה מזה מספר שנים.
האירוע הנוכחי מגיע בעיתוי נפיץ במיוחד: רק ביום ראשון האחרון הודיע המשרד להגנת הסביבה כי הוא מאשר את חידוש עבודות השיפוץ והתחזוקה בגדיב. האישור ניתן לאחר שהמפעל השלים דרישות בעקבות חריגות בנזן קודמות שהובילו אז להשבתת בתי ספר סמוכים ולהנחיות מיוחדות לתושבים. במשרד הדגישו אז כי למפעל הוצא צו מנהלי מעודכן הכולל שלושה מנגנוני בקרה (תפעולי, בגדר המפעל וסביבתי) שנועדו להבטיח עצירה מיידית במקרה של עלייה במדדים כדי למנוע חריגות. ואולם, בשטח התברר כי המנגנונים לא הצליחו למנוע את החריגה היממתית אלא הביאו לעצירת העבודות רק בדיעבד - לאחר שהתושבים כבר נחשפו לחומר המסרטן.
המשרד להגנת הסביבה הודיע כי הורה אמש על הפסקת עבודות התחזוקה במפעל גדיב שבמתחם בז"ן, בעקבות החריגה בריכוזי הבנזן שנמדדו בתחנת הניטור בשכונת קריית בנימין בק

Kenya has recorded a second Ebola death, the Health Ministry said on Friday.
Officials identified the patient as a 65-year-old woman, a close relative of a Kenyan man who died of Ebola earlier this month.
The woman began showing symptoms 10 days ago while in quarantine. She began receiving supportive care at an infectious disease unit in the capital, Nairobi.
"Sadly, she succumbed to the disease early this evening," the ministry said.
Medical personnel "did everything possible to save her life," the ministry said, adding that it had notified her family and would arrange a safe and dignified burial in consultation with relatives.
Seven people continue to receive treatment for the illness in Kenya.
What else do we know about the 2nd Kenyan Ebola death?
Kenya's first Ebola case was announced on October 6. The virus was found in a 40-year-old Kenyan man living in Congo, who travelled to Kenya via Uganda, arriving on October 3.
He tested positive for the disease on October 5 and died on the same day.
Of some 135 who were identified as contacts with the patient, 118 were placed in quarantine, with eight testing positive. They included four health workers and four close family members.
The remaining seven cases are all within "one cluster, with no evidence of community spread", the ministry added.

Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease.
A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said.
Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added.

Source: The Guardian World
Title: India slashes cost of cancer drugs after court rules mark-ups are ‘extortion’
URL: https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/23/india-cuts-cost-cancer-drugs
Published: 2026-10-23T07:00:03+00:00
Content: full article text

The Indian government has moved to reduce the price of cancer drugs after a retired bank clerk took her case to the supreme court.
From next month, 137 cancer drugs in India will be cheaper as the government tries to tackle the tragedy of poorer patients either forgoing treatment, selling land or falling into debt to meet the high cost of some medicines, which are making large profits for hospitals and pharmacists.
Sarojam Radhakrishnan, a former bank employee in Kerala, was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2021. Doctors prescribed life-saving targeted treatments but the monthly cost, of more than 63,000 rupees (£500), was far beyond her family’s means.
Realising that thousands of families were being ruined by the cost of such drugs, Radhakrishnan filed a petition to the Kerala high court in 2022 demanding government intervention to lower the costs.
When the case reached the supreme court, the judges looked at hospitals’ and retailers’ mark-ups on cancer drugs and called the situation “carnage” and “extortion”.
During a hearing on 29 September, justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta noted how a life-saving cancer drug supplied to hospitals at 2,700 rupees carried a vastly marked-up price of 27,000 rupees.
The judges found that hospitals, distributors and chemists enjoyed large margins on medicines. Analysis by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority revealed a trade mark-up on some cancer drugs averaging 170%, with some extreme examples stretching to more than 700%.
A 30% trade margin cap on the price of 42 drugs has been in place for some years but many others remained off this list. Now, prodded by the supreme court’s findings, the government has imposed the cap on 137 other drugs.
“The measure is expected to reduce medicine prices by up to 70% and help cancer patients save 2,500 crore rupees [£199m] annually, significantly reducing the amount they pay from their own pockets,” a statement from the Department of Pharmaceuticals said.
People on low incomes in India dread illness, as the cost of treatment can mean financial ruin, particularly for cancer patients.
Whenever the Indian Cancer Society holds a free diagnosis camp in Gurgaon where he lives, Krishan Kalra urges local drivers, maids, cooks and tailors to turn up because tests they cannot afford are offered free.
As a former member of the council of the Rajiv Gandhi Cancer Institute and Research Centre, Kalra knows the importance of early diagnosis, but he said very few people attended. “When I ask why, they say they’re too scared – if something serious like cancer is detected, they haven’t got the money to pay for the treatment so they prefer to remain in the dark,” he said.
With the cost of cancer drugs ranging in price from 38,000 to 380,000 rupees, many families quietly walk out of the doctor’s consulting room upon hearing the estimated cost of treatment.
Studies by the Public Health Foundation of India show that spending on healthcare pushes about 55 million Indians a year below the poverty line.
Few Indians can afford the premiums for comprehensive health insurance. The government’s nationwide insurance scheme, Ayushman Bharat, covers treatment for some cancers but it provides only 500,000 rupees’ worth of annual cover for a family – the cost of just one dose of Kadcyla (ado-trastuzumab emtansine), a drug used to treat breast cancer. Patients may need up to 14 doses.
Dr Ravi Kannan is a surgical oncologist and director of Cachar cancer hospital and research centre in Silchar, Assam. He has worked in hospitals elsewhere in India and is familiar with doctors’ trauma of seeing patients walk out to go home and die.
